The left-arm seamer, with 13 wickets from 10 matches at an economy rate of 8.20, is in the running for the purple cap.

There were initial doubts over Zaheer's fitness but in the tournament, he has taken up the task of spearheading the Royal Challengers' bowling department with considerable ease. Although he picked up a wicket in his very first match, he also went for runs. In his second match, he returned with enviable figures of 4-1-7-2, mixing up yorker-length deliveries with slower ones, surprising many a batsmen. Only in the last match against the Rajasthan Royals at Jaipur, he went wicket-less and proved expensive, conceding 46 runs in his four overs.

With a few other contenders for the purple cap, Zaheer will have to return to his best against the Delhi Daredevils. He is currently behind Shane Warne (14 wickets) and is tied with Irfan Pathan and S Sreesanth, who are ahead on average.

Another performer in the Bangalore ranks is skipper Rahul Dravid. Despite controversies and pressure, Dravid has delivered as a batsman. His unbeaten 36-ball 75 on Saturday may have gone in vain, but Dravid has silenced those who felt he was unfit for T20.

But Dravid's needs to rise as a skipper too. He needs to infuse in them a spirit that is lacking.

"I expected them to do better than they have. It's a very good team, capable of doing much better. The likes of Kallis, Chanderpaul and Dravid are the best in the world," said Delhi Daredevils' AB de Villiers.

Heading: ACU warns SRK, asks him to stay out of player’s dug-out - Indian Express
Content:
One fine tickle down the legside for four runs from the experienced Stephen Fleming, and an inexcusable dropped chance from Ashok Dinda in the outfield were decisive as Chennai Super Kings won the rain-hit match by two runs on D/L method at Eden Gardens to push hosts Kolkata Knight Riders further down the league table.

Chasing a modest 150 for victory after Makhaya Ntini (4/21) dominated a slow-low Eden wicket with a hat-trick, MS Dhoni & Co raced to 55 for no loss off eight overs when a thunderstorm lashed the Eden, washing out the all-important clash. Fleming's 20-ball cameo, which fetched him 32 runs, turned out to be the difference between the two sides.

Soon after the thunderstorm, calculators were out and match officials swung into action and declared that the visitors, ahead by three runs on the Duckworth-Lewis method, were the winners, leaving the hapless Kolkata Knight Riders to kicking themselves for messing up the crucial eighth over of Super Kings' chase. Today's win virtually put Chennai Super Kings in the semi-finals

Little did Ajit Agarkar realise that his second over would be the turning point of the match. Eight runs came off the eighth and last over of the curtailed match, and local boy Dinda dropped a sitter fourth ball of Parthiv Patel (19 not out) at long-off. The next ball saw Fleming gliding a straying Agarkar down the leg-side fence, which proved to be decisive. The southpaw duo of Fleming and Patel (55 runs off 8 overs) neatly went about the chase and even Shoaib Akhtar couldn't recreate the magic of the last match, giving 14 runs off his two overs.

The Knight Riders got off to yet another sluggish start, and for the umpteenth time in the IPL, Sourav Ganguly & Co choked on the run-rate front. After an unimpressive start—they were 28/2 after 5 overs—John Buchanan's boys were crippled by a delayed hat-trick from the intimidating Ntini before eventually recovering to a respectable 149/5 off 20 overs. After several failures, Salman Butt finally made his knock count for at the top of the order, carving out a hard-fought 73 off 54 balls. But for him and local boy Debabrata Das (27 runs off 32 balls), the Kolkata team would have had a tougher time. The duo added 86 off 67 balls for the third wicket, before the deadly Ntini came back in his last spell to end the partnership that was studded with some lusty hits from Butt and the little-known Bengal boy.

Skipper Ganguly couldn't inspire yet again on his home turf, departing for a miserable two off eight balls. And that dismissal was the beginning of the tournament's third hat-trick. Returning with figures of 4 wickets for 21 runs, Ntini's hat-trick is Chennai Super Kings' second in the tournament after Laxmipathy Balaji, with Delhi Daredevils' Amit Mishra registering the other one.

After knocking down Ganguly's middle-stump off the last ball of his third over—Kolkata were 28/2 in 5 overs—Ntini came back for the second spell in the 17th over and cleaned up Das and David Hussey (0) off the first two balls to complete a well-deserved hat-trick. Interestingly, the tournament's third hat-trick came in a delayed effort, and the entire crowd missed it for a long while, including the official scorer at the Eden.

Heading: ‘Sitting out just takes away form’ - Indian Express
Content:
Known to play to the gallery at the IPL matches with his entertaining antics and electric presence, SRK was today literally snubbed by the International Cricket Council's (ICC) chief security officer, in charge of monitoring matters related to anti-corruption measures. Niranjan Singh Virk, the ICC's Anti-Corruption and Security Unit (ACSU) officer at today's IPL match, ordered the Bollywood superstar on his face to keep out of the players' dressing room and the dugouts in the course of the match.

Shah Rukh himself admitted to the caution later in the evening, the Kolkata team owner admitted to being cautioned by Virk. "I was told about the rule by the concerned officer. It's not an issue, but I have decided not to enter the players' dressing room from now," SRK said. Interestingly, ever since the IPL carnival began, Kolkata franchise owner Shah Rukh has been cheering his team on from the stands, the dug-outs, on the fence and occasionally dropping by in the players' dressing room to egg them on and advice them.

CAB insiders narrated the unsavoury turn of events to The Indian Express demanding anonymity, and admitted that SRK was miffed at being told to stay out of the dressing room and the dugout. "Shah Rukh occasionally drops in at the dressing room just to have a light chit-chat with the players. And today he sat alongside the players at the dugout. But the ICC's anti-corruption is very strict with matters like these.

When Shah Rukh was told not to enter the dressing room, he felt insulted and hurt, but immediately agreed to follow the ICC officer's advice.

There's no problem now. When the ICC officer learnt that Shah Rukh is the team owner, he softened his stand," revealed a reliable CAB source.

Since the IPL is played under ICC guidelines, the apex body has been strict about posting anti-corruption officers at the matches. And with the disciplinarian Virk getting involved in today's episode, it brought back memories of last November when the same ICC officer had asked CAB's guest Mohammad Azharuddin to keep out of the dressing room at Eden during the India-Pakistan Test match.

Heading: China row: BJP says UPA inactive, Left warns against ‘provocation’ - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani left-hander Salman Butt came down heavily on coach John Buchanan, captain Sourav Ganguly & the rest of the team think-tank for trying far too many opening combinations during batting.

"It's a good question to those who decide the batting order," said a clearly sarcastic Butt, making a guarded but distinct reference to the Kolkata Knight Riders think-tank.

"I came here on the back of some good knocks in Pakistan and, when in form, everybody loves to play. Sitting out just takes the form away," Butt rued, referring to the team management's decision to try seven opening combinations in the 11 matches so far.

Heading: PM calls on ailing Surjeet, doctors say he is critical - Indian Express
Content:
With China making fresh claims on Indian soil at the northernmost tip of Sikkim, the BJP on Sunday hit out strongly at the Congress-led UPA government for "not doing enough" to check the "expansionist designs" of China.

While the Indian Government struck a more reconciliatory note despite China's stridency on the issue, the ruling Congress sought to distance itself as it said there was no "question of any territorial claims" since that had been resolved decades ago.

The Left, on its part, said both countries should not take "provocative steps" while the talks on border dispute are still underway.

The BJP — a day after The Sunday Express reported on the Chinese fresh claims and troop entry into the "finger area" which is the northernmost tip of Sikkim — slammed the Left-backed, Congress-led UPA Government. "First it was Arunachal Pradesh, and now it's Sikkim. We would like the Union Government to tell us what it is doing to check the increasing and frequent Chinese incursions on the Indian side," said BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad.

Former External Affairs Minister and senior BJP leader Yashwant Sinha, too, reacted strongly to the incursion. "The UPA Government has been supine in the face of the growing Chinese threat. The Government has allowed domestic politics, with the disproportionate influence of CPM, to influence its foreign policy."

The Government sources shared their concern at the Chinese claims, especially in the finger area, since "it is a demarcated area" since 1890. "Patrols have crossed traditionally, since 1959—- they have crossed the line, even our patrolling teams have crossed. There's a system to sort it out at the ground level. We would like this to be sorted out there, and if it's not possible there, it will be taken up at a suitably higher level."

Congress party spokesperson Manish Tewari said it would be appropriated if the Ministry of External Affairs or the Ministry of Defence commented on it. "As far as we are concerned, as we understand, Sikkim was integrated into India in 1974 in consonance with the wishes of the Sikkimese people. There were never any outstanding issues between the erstwhile Princely State of Sikkim and the People's Republic of China. China recognized unconditionally the integration of Sikkim into India. Therefore, the question of any territorial claims, if made at all, does not exist."

CPI National Secretary D Raja said, "There are some border disputes between the two countries and talks are taking place to resolve them. Let us hope both sides reasonably settle the dispute. No sides should take any provocative steps when the talks are on."

However, BJP led the charge against the Left-backed, Congress-led UPA's ruling coalition, as Ravi Shankar Prasad said, "During former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee's visit, China had recognized Sikkim as an integral part of India. How are they then laying claim on Finger Area? How come the Chinese ambassador has not been summoned so far? And why hasn't the Union Government lodged a formal protest as yet."

Yashwant Sinha too joined the BJP's strident criticism of the government's attitude. "We should have given them a proper response on Arunachal Pradesh, their summoning our ambassador at 2 am, and even issues that embarrass the Chinese, like Tibet. The Chinese, however, think that they can needle India at will and get away with it, because it's the UPA Government at the helm," Sinha added.

Heading: Cong is playing the game of caste politics: L K Advani - Indian Express
Content:
Senior Marxist leader Harkishan Singh Surjeet, 93, continued to be critical on Sunday after lapsing into a coma on Saturday. Doctors examining him at the Metro hospital in Noida are of the opinion that chances of his survival are minimal.

"According to our previous experiences, patients [of his age] do not make it for long... his condition is critical," said Dr Purushotam Lal, Chief Cardiologist, Metro Hospital.

Surjeet, who was admitted to the Metro Heart Institute in Noida on May 6 with high fever and a lung infection, had to be put on ventilator on Thursday when his condition deteriorated after the food he was eating passed into his lungs. "He has been admitted to the hospital on numerous occasions, but this time it's

serious since he suffered a cardio-respiratory arrest, after which needed a cardiac massage and supportive treatment," explained Dr Lal.

On Sunday, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh visited the hospital and spoke to the doctors about the veteran leader's condition. Prakash Karat also came to check on his well-being. Doctors confirmed that Surjeet has not shown much improvement. "Some parameters are stable but the situation is very unpredictable. It's a wait and watch situation," added another doctor.

Surjeet has already been admitted to the hospital about 15-20 times this year. This time, doctors fear that he may have suffered irreversible brain damage even though hye continues to blink and react to painful stimuli.

Heading: India to not let Jaipur blasts derail talks with Pak - Indian Express
Content:
Campaigning in one of the most backward regions in the state, former deputy prime minister and senior BJP leader L K Advani on Sunday termed Congress' reluctance to name its chief ministerial candidate for the Assembly polls as an example of caste politics. "The Congress has fielded probable candidates from different castes, hoping that people from all castes will vote for the party. This is caste politics and I don't agree with it," Advani said.

He addressed a fairly large gathering at Nehru Stadium in Hubli City, in north of Karnataka — what is known as the Bombay-Karnataka region — where the BJP has been consistently increasing its vote share in the last two decades. The party hopes to form government on its own in Karnataka.

With the impoverished districts in the region heavily dependent on agriculture and prone to droughts, BJP's campaign focused on farming issues and skirted issues like terrorism that was central to its earlier campaigning. "The biggest failure of the UPA Government has been in controlling the price rise and the worst affected are the farmers," Advani said.

Heading: The Janata days, fights relived - Indian Express
Content:
In its first high-level political engagement with the new Pakistan government, India will not let the recent Jaipur blasts "derail" the India-Pakistan talks to be held in Islamabad on May 20 and 21, Ministry of External Affairs sources said today.

Though India will raise concerns about cross-border terrorism during the high-level meetings between External Affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee and the top Pakistani leadership, including President Pervez Musharraf , it is hoping to forge the dialogue "with an open mind and positive framework."

As investigations into the Jaipur blasts are still underway, India doesn't want to "pre-judge" the situation, say sources, adding that it logical to assume that the perpetrators of the terror acts would want the talks between the two countries to be marred. "We don't want to lend victory to forces, which are aiming at derailing the peace process between the two countries," a source said. However, dates for the next meeting of the India-Pakistan anti-terror mechanism are expected to set during the bilateral meetings.

Ahead of the talks, meanwhile, Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon, said on Sunday, "The dialogue process has contributed meaningfully to the improvement of relations over the last four years. India is ready to carry the process forward."

External Affairs ministry sources said the two countries are aiming at a "bigger economic relationship", as has been evident from recent statements made by Pakistan People's Party co-chairman Asif Zardari, the man who has the keys to the present Pakistan government. The meeting will discuss the issues of "economic cooperation" between the two countries.

Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon and his Pakistani counterpart, Salman Bashir, will mainly focus on "peace and security" and "Jammu and Kashmir" as a part of the review of the fourth round of composite dialogue between the two countries. The meeting between Menon and Bashir, where both sides will begin by "picking up the threads", will take place in Islamabad on May 20.

Sources said the bilateral talks will be more of a familiarization exercise for the India side, where the Indian delegation will be "keen to know the views" of the newly-elected three-month-old Pakistan government on all the key issues, which are being discussed under the "composite dialogue" process.

India will raise "all concerns" during the Indo-Pak talks, the MEA sources said, with regard to all eight issues, which include Siachen and Sir Creek. "And then, we will see what the Pakistan leaders have to say," the source said.

MEA also doesn't want to single out the Sarabjit Singh case, and instead, wants to talk about all Indian prisoners in Pakistani jails. "As far as we are concerned, there will be talk about the condition of prisoners, in an overall sense, which will include Sarabjit Singh's case," official sources said.

Heading: Plans to extend mobile reach to borders to tackle signal spillover - Indian Express
Content:
Late for a Cabinet Committee meeting sometime in 1978, Charan Singh was unusually apologetic as he greeted his colleagues. "I'm sorry; I got held up due to a journalist," he told them while working on a blueprint on electoral reforms. L K Advani, Shanti Bhushan and P C Chunder were the other members, besides Singh, on the committee.

Union Law Minister in the Janata regime Shanti Bhushan asked him to take it easy though. "The reporter asked me if I wanted to become the Prime Minister. I told him that the people who don't aim high are no good. But how can I be interested in the job when Morarjibhai is around. I'm, of course, available once he's dead," said Singh as his colleagues were left speechless.

When Shanti Bhushan later narrated the incident to Morarji, the PM had something more interesting to say. "An astrologer recently told me that a couple of my colleagues, both around 75, may soon die," he said. Two ministers, in the said age-bracket in the Cabinet then were Charan Singh and Jagjivan Ram, both potential challengers for the PM's post.

Shanti Bhushan, who had played a key role in putting together the Janata Government, under the guidance of Jayprakash Narayan, knew that the Government was on its last legs. "How could a Government, where ministers wished their colleagues nothing but death, be expected to last," he said, at a book-release function on the Janata experiment here on Sunday. The event saw the likes of George Fernandes, Rajnath Singh, I K Gujral and Raghuvansh Prasad Singh.

"We were working on electoral reforms that would have made the future elections transparent and inexpensive. The Naxalites and the poor today then could have fought the moneyed on an even kneel in elections," recalled Shanti Bhushan.

Bharatiya Janata Party president Rajnath Singh, who was barely 25 at the onset of Emergency, said that the repression and the subsequent fightback by democratic forces injected a dose of resilience in the polity. "The youth like us then thought that we could make the impossible come true. In a way, we have. The track record of the BJP, born only in 1980, makes others pale in comparison," said the BJP president.

Civil servant-turned politician Syed Shahabuddin recalled that there were at least three officers in Bihar besides him who didn't agree with Indira Gandhi's repressive order at all. While other speakers too had their own take on the era, it was the presence of George Fernandes at the book launch that captured the spirit of resistance to the Emergency in true measure.

George had been advised rest by his doctors. True to his image, George overruled them and made his presence felt, even though he didn't utter a word. "It dealt with the Emergency and the Janata experiment, and he couldn't have stayed away," the author later said. The book, "The Janata Enigma - 30 out of 60" has been written by journalist Kumar Rajesh and published by Manak Publications.

Heading: BJP questions PM’s commitment - Indian Express
Content:
India plans to expand the mobile phone reach along its border in a bid to counter the signal spillovers from Pakistan and Bangladesh that are aiding communication between terrorist modules and their masterminds across the border.

"By not providing mobile services near international border by Indian service providers, people in the border town feel alienated, they use mobile services of their neighbouring country and it is not possible to monitor traffic of such calls," says a proposal by the Department of Telecommunication.

The DoT has therefore recommended that mobile firms be allowed to install cell sites and radio transmitters within the 10-km buffer zone along the border, Line of Control and Line of Actual Control with the permission to expand service coverage to within 500 metres, presently a 'No Service Zone'.

In the proposal to the Committee of Secretaries which, in February 2007 allowed mobile services in frontier areas, the DoT has sought exemption on condition that signals would fade out when nearing or about to cross the border and also become unusable "within a reasonable distance across such border".

Last August, the External Affairs ministry was asked to take up the issue of signal spillovers with the neighbours but the diplomatic efforts came to a naught. "The matter has been taken up regularly with the Bangladesh government for removing communication towers and link stations adjacent to the border. However, the Bangladesh side has not responded so far to our request," it said.

The other option of installing jammers — with effective range of 3-4 km - was found to be 'practically impossible' as it would require numerous such jammers to create an electronic fence. Their operation and maintenance was also another handicap.

The BSF and other security agencies have reported that signals seeping into the country were often misused for trans-border crimes and were "an inherent risk for security and anti-India activities along the border".

The Intelligence Bureau too has favoured the proposal of installing base trans-receiver stations in the 10-km radius of LAC, LOC and the international border between Akhnoor and Pathankot "provided the usable signal is not available within the 500-metres zone."

Citing gross violation by service providers, the IB has suggested that "DoT should put in place a monitoring mechanism to ensure and assure the security agencies that the service providers strictly follow the conditions of restricting the usable signals 500 metres short of the border and that the subscriber verification is reliable".

But the Ministry of Defence is opposed to it saying that any further relaxation would result in "adverse security implications". The present buffer zone, it said, was helping thwart attempts by terrorists in crossing the border as well as the anti-infiltration operation of the security forces "as lack of useable mobile signals in this zone considerably increases the vulnerability of terrorists."

Heading: Congress resignations a political stunt: Badal - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Prime Minister Manmohan Singh pitched for a federal crime agency, the BJP on Sunday questioned his commitment to fight terror and said a new agency would be of no use unless it is armed with a POTA-type stringent anti-terror law. "Manmohan Singh's bonafides in the war against terror are suspect," senior BJP leader Arun Jaitley said, while asking whether a federal agency under him to deal with terror crimes can really be trusted given his "track record" in the last four years.

"It is ironical that after being in prime ministerial office for four years the Prime Minister has finally woken up to the harsh and cruel reality that prevention and investigation of terrorism in India is on the verge of collapse," Jaitley said.

He said the repeal of POTA, not giving assent to similar anti-terror laws in BJP-ruled states, non-execution of Parliament attack convict Afzal Guru and "helping the accused being prosecuted under POTA for burning Sabarmati Express" raises a legitimate question whether a federal agency under Singh can really be trusted.

Jaitley asked, "does the Prime Minister's track record inspire confidence that he will implement his proposal for a federal agency against terror."

He also sought to know whether Singh will have the political courage to strengthen the content of India's anti-terrorist laws to make them more "terrorist-unfriendly".

Claiming that the Prime Minister and Congress had been opposing strong anti-terror law, he sought to know "will not the federal agency be helpless in investigating terrorist crimes if confessions of terrorists are inadmissible evidence and an easy bail is available to the terrorists under normal law".

Heading: After recent infiltration, Govt tells nomads to avoid traditional routes - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the resignations of Congress MLAs merely a political stunt aimed at seeking publicity, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on Sunday dared the Congress leadership in the state to forward their resignations to the Vidhan Sabha Speaker.

Speaking at Rakhra village, Badal said the Congress party has resorted to cheap publicity — an outcome of their frustrations in the wake of their complete rout in the Assembly elections. The results of the civic polls and now the panchayat and ZP polls, he said, had a negative impact on the Congress, which was now trying to save its face. Badal further said, "stuntmanship is no substitute to statesmanship, as Congress has resorted to cheap theatricals", adding that by doing so the state Congress was trying to save its face before its high command and avoid embarrassment.

The CM was here to attend the Bhog ceremony of Jaswant Kaur, the mother of Akali leader Surjit Singh Rakhra and NRI businessman Darshan Singh Dhaliwal, who had died in Chicago a few days ago.

Badal said the Congress was fighting a losing battle in Punjab, as it had been suffering one defeat after the other in various polls held in the state. "Similar would be the outcome of the Parliamentary polls", said Badal.

The Akali leader said Bhattal was only doing such "stunts" to remain in the news and gain some cheap publicity. Regarding the announcement of the gherao of his residence by PPCC on May 24, the CM said Bhattal was his neighbour and had been meeting him many times. Regarding SAD's victory in recent ZP and Block Samiti polls in Punjab, particularly in the Malwa belt from where SAD faced a complete rout in the last assembly polls, he said that it was the state Government's performance during the past few months that had translated into votes.

Heading: In Alphonso land, huge shortage of export-quality mangoes - Indian Express
Content:
The recent infiltration and spurt in militant activities has not only made authorities, police and armed forced wary of attacks in the state ahead of the polls and the Amarnath yatra, the government for the first time has restricted movements of the nomads of the Gujjars-Bakerwal tribes to the upper reaches of the Himalayas.

Nearly two lakh nomads of the two tribes, along with their cattle, migrate to the higher reaches each summer. But as a precautionary measure, official sources said, they have been asked not to taker their traditional routes which is also accessed by militants.

Inspector General of Police, Jammu zone, K Rajendra Kumar said that such measures have been taken in order to ensure safety and security of these people.

The nomads have fixed official routes for migration, around seven of them, which are decided by the government. However, there are other routes too — almost 15, including the seven official routes, — for which the migrants are given permits.

But some of these migratory routes are unsafe as they are often taken by militants.

And these routes fall along both the Line of Control (LoC) and the International Border.

Last week, around four to five militants according to the Border Security Force chief might have sneaked into India from the International Border in the Samba sector. Around eight people were killed and more than a dozen injured in the last night firing.

Heading: Relatives of girls killed in Bodeli demand compensation from GSRTC - Indian Express
Content:
Raju Tamhankar was eagerly looking forward to the summer of 2008. The mango farmer in Maharashtra's Ratnagiri district had got his farm certified under the stringent Global Good Agricultural Practices norms and was aiming to export half his annual produce of 24,000 fruits to the United States. After all, this was the first full mango season open to exports to the lucrative US market after Washington lifted a 18-year ban last year.

However, what Tamhankar and scores of fellow mango farmers across Alphonso land in the Konkan region had not accounted for was a double freak phenomena. Probably for the first time in half a century, the trees flowered twice — in November and January — instead of just once in November, affecting the quantity of output. And then, the crop was battered by heavy unseasonal rains in March. The result: a huge shortage of good quality Alphonso. "The target was to export 12,000 mangoes, but now I am struggling," said Tamhankar, adding that efforts to get the Euro quality certificates seem to have been such a waste. "It's like reaching the doors of US and having to return due to the bad produce."

Sachin Langekar, a large mango farmer with 5,000 trees across Ratnagiri, Devgarh and Vijaydurg, said 20 exporters had placed orders before the season began but he has been able to supply only three so far. "The month of May is supposed to be the busiest for us. But we are sitting idle because quality mangoes are not available to export," he said.

India, the world's largest producer of the golden fruit, began exporting it to the United States in April last year following years of lobbying in what some analysts have called "mango diplomacy" while others labeled it "mangoes for motorcycles" as India simultaneously allowed the import of the legendary Harley-Davidson bikes. Washington had refused to accept the fruit shipments in the past because they were not irradiated to protect against fruit flies and pests. New Delhi agreed to the measures as part of ongoing moves by the two countries to forge closer ties. Under the conditions agreed for export, the fruit has to be spotless and weigh between 225 gm and 300 gm each. But the double flowering and rains meant much of this year's crop fulfilled neither condition with the unfavourable weather resulting in black spots or fungal diseases.

"With the hype around Alphonso and other Indian mangoes and the large market, we had projected exports of at least 1,500 metric tonnes. But so far, we have exported just 80 metric tonnes," said Ranjit Mondal, Mumbai head of the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA).

The shortfall has presented another problem for the apex body of exporters. It fears that some farmers or exporters could try to get around the shortage by shipping bad quality fruits. "We have told them to be careful when it comes to exporting the mangoes. It is better not to send the fruit than to earn a bad name for the country by sending poor quality," Mondal said.

While some exporters are using the opportunity to ship other varieties such as Kesar and Rajapuri, APEDA is planning to organise mango promotions in Europe and the U.S. this month and the next to open a window to a world beyond the Alphonso. "People do not know about other varieties of Indian mangoes," Mondal said. "With these shows, we aim to educate customers, exporters and the market about different types of Indian mangoes."

Heading: Deshmukh must rein in Raj, says AICC secy - Indian Express
Content:
A month after the Bodeli mishap, parents of the 15 girls at Bamroli village have filed a petition at the Vadodara District Court and demanded compensation from Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC). Forty-one children died on April 16 when a State Transport Bus plunged into the Narmada canal near Bodeli.

The state government and the Education department announced a compensation of Rs 1 lakh and Rs 50,000 respectively, soon after the accident. Incidentally, 15 of the children were girl students from Bamroli village, which had the highest number of casualties in the accident.

Vipin Pandya, an advocate of parents of the deceased from Bamroli said, "On May 14, parents of the 15 girls filed a petition to the District Court and demanded a compensation of Rs 5 lakh." He said, "even as the state appointed committee is yet to prove the cause of mishap, it is quite evident that mishap occurred due to the negligence on the part of the GSRTC."

"Under the Motor Vehicles Act, it is the owner of the vehicle, in this case the GSRTC, which has to indemnify for the negligence of driver," said Pandya.

"There cannot be any proceedings against the driver, since he also died in the mishap. In such a condition, it is the owner of the vehicle which has to make amends for the death of the relative who has filed the petition in the court," he added.

Sources in Bodeli, meanwhile, said that families of the deceased from other villages are also planning to file a suit against GSRTC.

Abhaysinh Baria whose two daughters Renuka and Raksha died in the accident said, "It was three days ago, that I, along with 14 other parents whose children died in the mishap went to the Vadodara District Civil Court to file a petition seeking compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act."

Heading: NC Hills violence: Oppn slams state Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Senior Congress leader and AICC secretary Anil Shastri said on Sunday tough measures should be taken against Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray in view of his continuous hate campaign against North Indians in Maharashtra, particularly Mumbai.

"Maharashtra Government should have arrested Thackeray earlier itself but may be due to local constraints it was unable to do so. Now, however, the time has come for it to rein in the MNS leader," Shastri told reporters.

"His comments against North Indians, specially against Amitabh Bachchan are highly condemnable and therefore, the Maharashtra Government should take strict action against him," Shastri said.

Shastri was here to take part in a programme of the Kayastha community.

As regards the issue of alliance, he said it would not be in the interest of the Congress in the long run. "It is necessary for the party to stand on its own in states like Uttar Pradesh. One cannot stand for a longer period with the help of crutches," he said. However, he added that any decision in this regard will be taken by the senior party leadership.

When asked whether the Congress Party will contest the general elections on its own or with UPA, he said that UPA is not a long term arrangement.

Heading: Both Dispur and Delhi ignore Assam hill district: leader - Indian Express
Content:
The opposition parties on Sunday criticised the Congress-led state Government for its silence regarding violence in North Cachar Hills district. As many as 25 people were gunned down by militants during the past week in the district.

"So many innocent persons have been killed in the past week. Two major national projects, involving both the railways and NHAI, have come to a halt. The railways have not only suspended train services through the district but also evacuated all its employees and their families. Yet, not a single line statement has been issued by the state Government," said Brindaban Goswami, president of Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), after a meeting of leaders of non-Congress parties here on Sunday.

Goswami added: "The Chief Minister is away. Two most important officers of the district — Deputy

Commissioner and SP — are on leave. The DGP and Chief Secretary have not even uttered a single word on this tragedy."

Leaders of eight opposition parties, including the AGP, CPI, CPI(M), BJP, ASDC, NCP, and Bodo People's Front, who discussed the lawlessness and state Government's inaction in the North Cachar Hills district, urged the Prime

Minister and the Union Home Minister to immediately intervene before the situation worsens.

"While we condemn the militants for having unleashed a reign of terror in the district, we also hold the Congress-led state Government equally responsible for the lawlessness prevailing in the district," Goswami said.

Militants belonging to the Jewel Gorlosa faction of Dima Halam Daogah (DHD), better known as Black Widow, have targeted and killed employees of contractors engaged by the railways and NHAI and also killed two railway employees in the past one week. Ten truck drivers on contract with a cement company were also gunned down.

A prominent leader of the Baite community, who had raised his voice against the violence, was killed on Friday.

Heading: Army apprehensive of toll plaza near ammunition depot - Indian Express
Content:
The Deputy Commissioner is on leave on health grounds, and the Superintendent of Police has gone abroad for training, "but even when they are here, the two top officers of the district hardly respond to what we say," complained Depolal Hojai, Chief Executive Member of the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council (NCHAC), here on Sunday.

The NCHAC is the elected local government that runs the administration of the hill district under the provisions of the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, with Hojai of the Autonomous State Demand Committee (ASDC), a regional political party, heading the Council.

"But even as we run the local government, the responsibility for maintaining law and order is vested with the State Government under the Sixth Schedule. But whenever there is any problem in the district, they tend to put the blame on us," Hojai told The Indian Express here today. Hojai, whose ASDC party runs the Autonomous Council in coalition with the BJP, added that the Deputy Commissioner and SP also disregard the recommendations of the Autonomous Council on matters of law and order.

"While the law and order situation in the NC Hills has gone from bad to worse in the past few weeks, our feeling is that the Congress-led government in Dispur is happy over it. We had defeated and wrested the Autonomous Council from the Congress in the January elections. That is the reason why the state Government is not responding to us," he said.

Ever since militants belonging to the Black Widow or DHD(J) group caused havoc in the hill district by targeting employees and contractors of the Indian Railways and the NHAI, the railways have suspended all operations in the NC Hills and have also evacuated its employees from there. As a result, work on two vital national projects—the broad-gauge track between Lumding and Silchar and the East-West Corridor—have come to a standstill. Yet, both Dispur and Delhi do not seem to bother, Hojai said.

The Lumding-Silchar Hill Section is like a lifeline for Barak Valley in southern Assam as well as for Mizoram, Tripura and south Manipur, with essential commodities including foodgrains and cement being transported by the railways through the single metre gauge track. On an average, six trains run between Lumding and Badarpur every day to transport various kinds of essential commodities.

These include four goods trains that, between them, carry about 2,880 tonnes of foodgrains, one rake of petroleum products, as well as sugar, cement, bitumen and raw materials for the HPC paper mill at Panchgram.

Heading: Nagaland Govt gets UN public service award - Indian Express
Content:
In a clear violation of the guidelines laid down by the Ministry of Defence, the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) is constructing a 60-feet high toll plaza in front of the Dappar Ammunition Depot, one of India's biggest ammunition storehouses.

NHAI says it will get more revenue by constructing the collection centre at the point on the Chandigarh-New Delhi highway. The Army however, says it is a threat to the security of the ammunition depot as it is coming up in the notified area where raising any other structure is prohibited. According to the notification issued by the MoD in 2004, land lying within a distance of 1,200 yards (1,097.28 metres) from the crest of the outer parapet of the ammunition depot in Dappar, should be kept free from any obstruction. The former Mohali deputy commissioner has already reported the matter to the Punjab and Haryana High Court, after measuring the distance between the outer parapet of the ammunition depot and the toll plaza. It came out to be 830 metres.

Heading: NPCIL omits ‘import’, ‘shutdown’ from n-fuel records - Indian Express
Content:
Nagaland Government has won the United Nations' Public Service Awards for promoting community participation by handing over the ownership and management of schools, hospitals, electricity, water supply and tourism to the villagers.

The award which falls under the category of fostering participation in policy-making decisions through innovative mechanism would be given on June 23 at New York, the CM's office said in a release. Nagaland is the only winner in Asia Pacific region. It is one of the 12 awards given globally by the UN in various areas of public services. The announcement was communicated to the CM's office by Steel Secretary and former Nagaland Chief Secretary R S Pandey.

Heading: NEW WINE & OLD BOTTLE - Indian Express
Content:
The gravity of nuclear fuel shortage is something the country's nuclear power establishment would never openly admit. The Indo-US nuclear deal was expected to ease the situation and make imports of fuel possible so that our existing plants could be run at higher capacity rather than the average 40-50 per cent PLF, on account of shortages. But given the current stalemate on the Indo-US nuclear deal, and with fresh indigenous supplies not forthcoming, the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has been forced to change its position and has got words such as "import" of fuel, "shutting of units" deleted from recorded minutes on the status of their upcoming nuclear units.

Two new units at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (RAPS) (unit 5 and 6) should have both become operational by February this year. However, crippled by fuel shortages, the NPCIL has been deliberately going slow on these units and is now not firm on when Unit 6 would start operations.

In a meeting of northern regional power committee — an official body comprising all stakeholders of the northern power grid — in January this year, the NPCIL officials said "RAPP unit 5 reactor would be critical by January 08" and that "work has been started at some uranium mines, and within a few months, situation in terms of fuel availability would improve".

They even said, "Initially, for running unit 5 of RAPP, some other running unit may need to be shutdown."

In a similar meet of the committee earlier this week (May 12), the NPCIL changed its position and asked for an amendment in the same paragraph to read, "Trial run operation has been started at new uranium mine and within a few months, situation in terms of fuel availability would improve and RAPP unit-5 reactor would be made critical at the earliest."

The commitment of the reactor going critical by January 8 and that the initial running of unit 5 might require other unit "shutdown" has been dropped.

That is not all. The NPCIL was a bit more candid on the criticality of import of fuel and in the January meet. They informed the committee on why the new units at RAPP were delayed. They said, "Commissioning of RAPP units got delayed due to fuel problem. There is a teething problem at equipment level, manpower and import of fuel. Indigenous efforts are being made and gradual improvement is taking place. By the end of December, some product would be available for existing as well as future units."

But as the deadlock on the nuclear deal continued, in the May meet of the same committee, the NPCIL proposed another change in its earlier position and stated "Commissioning of RAPP-5 unit got delayed due to mismatch in fuel requirement and fuel supply. There are teething problems in fuel supply. Efforts are being made to improve the fuel supply position and gradual improvement is taking place."

In the change, the NPCIL narrowed the fuel shortage problem to unit 5, with no commitment on other units. "Fuel problem" is referred to as "mismatch" and there is no reference whatsoever to when "efforts" to improve fuel supply position are expected to pay dividends for their "existing" and "future units".

Heading: Defence auditors caught ‘taking paybacks’ in hotel - Indian Express
Content:
Although many nursed the hope that the Delhi Government would lower the legal drinking age from 25 to 21 this week, it was perhaps too much to ask in an election year. With the Sheila Dikshit Government saying a categorical "no go", the Capital retains its distinction of having one of the "highest" drinking age limits in the world. The important and much-debated question, of course, is: are such laws arbitrary? Do these actually help curb binge drinking, drunk-driving accidents or other alcohol-related problems? A look at drinking age laws of some other countries:

The United States Between 18 and 25

The US has uniformly the highest drinking age limit in the world (the legal drinking age varies between 18 and 25 across different states in India). According to the US National Underage Drinking Act of 1984, the age at which young people may start drinking alcohol across the country is 21. When certain states proposed reducing the limit to 18, the suggestion was met with public disapproval — a poll conducted by ABC News found that nearly eight in 10 Americans oppose lowering the drinking age in all states. Nonetheless, even though the US Department of Transportation insists that these laws have been instrumental in reducing traffic fatalities involving drivers between the ages of 18 and 20, the fact remains that between 1993 and 2001, this very age group showed the largest increase — 56 per cent — in binge drinking among American adults. In addition, 21 per cent of 16- to 20-year old drivers in fatal car accidents had enough alcohol in their systems to be considered legally impaired.

Mexico 18

With a drinking limit of 18, Mexico is a favourite destination for underage American revellers who pour into the border town of Tijuana by the thousands every weekend. The biggest public health concern this poses is that young drivers travelling between the two countries are often drunk. According to some sources, approximately 30 per cent of those who return to the US from Mexico between midnight and 6 am have dangerously high blood alcohol concentrations. These statistics add to the case for more lenient laws in the US.

The United Kingdom Below 18 can't purchase liquor

Although people under the age of 18 cannot purchase liquor, 16- and 17-year olds can be served cider, beer and wine in restaurants; they are required to be under adult supervision in England and Scotland, but not in Wales. Another somewhat bizarre law stipulates that it is acceptable to serve alcohol to a minor above five years of age, but only in homes and not in public places. Pint-sized closet drinkers apart, the UK is currently facing a serious problem with underage drinking -- for example, a study in Scotland found that around 68 per cent of 13-year-old children drank alcohol. A study by Alcohol Concern, a UK-based organisation, revealed that about one in five 11-year-olds admitted to drinking regularly.

France, Italy, Netherlands & Germany 16

Known for their permissiveness, these European countries share a minimum drinking age of 16, although there are distinctions made for the type of beverage: you have to be 18 or above to buy hard liquor in France, Germany and the Netherlands, although Italy has no such restrictions. A proposal to increase the minimum age in Italy to 18 was rejected by the parliament in 2007. The argument was that more relaxed laws "demystify" alcohol to youngsters and make them less likely to binge drink. However, a 1995 poll conducted by the US Department of Justice of 10th-grade students from America and Europe found that youngsters in Europe were actually more likely to drink and binge than in the relatively strict US.

New Zealand Lowered from 20 to 18

New Zealand presents what is perhaps the most dramatic case study illustrating the urgency of enforcing higher minimum-age drinking laws. The country lowered its minimum drinking age to 18 from 20 in 1999, and recent research suggests that this may have had a direct impact on the rising traffic casualties among young people. A 2006 study published in The American Journal of Public Health found that the rate of traffic crashes and injuries increased 12 per cent for 18- to 19-year-old males and 51 per cent for females of the same age.

Japan 20

The legal drinking age in Japan is 20, but just how effectively this drinking law is implemented is questionable, especially considering that it's one of the few countries in the world with alcohol-vending machines. However, as a response to public concern, the number of machines has now dropped owing to voluntary regulation by the alcohol industry as well as retailers.

Heading: Spurious liquor claims 21 lives - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Police's Detective Department claims to have caught six auditors of the Controller of Defence Accounts (CDA), Patna, with official documents, including bills for medical purchases made by the Command Hospital, Eastern Command, while reportedly holding "unauthorised" meetings with creditors at a Kolkata hotel 10 days ago.

However, in the absence of a complaint, they had to let them go after a few hours. The raid, carried out on May 9 at Hotel Savera in the New Market area following an intelligence tip-off, had caught the auditors red-handed settling bills of Kolkata-based pharma suppliers for a percentage kickback.

The CDA auditors, whose endorsement is required for payment of bills of suppliers to defence installations, had apparently come to Kolkata to expedite settlement of outstanding bills totalling Rs 1 crore.

Deputy Commissioner (Detective Department) Jawed Shamim said the lack of a formal complaint had tied the police's hands. "They are senior Central Government employees. An amount of Rs 5.4 lakh in cash among six persons is not unnaturally large. No complaint was lodged. "

Senior Auditor Ajay Kumar, however, denied any wrongdoing. "We had come to Kolkata to watch the IPL match. We left for Kolkata straight from office and those documents were carried by mistake due to the rush. As it was raining in Kolkata that day, we couldn't go for the match. The mentioned amount in cash was not in our possession," Kumar told The Indian Express from Patna.

Among the documents allegedly carried by the auditors was a letter signed by the Officer-In-Charge, Medical Stores, of the Eastern Command Hospital, Lt Col Anjani Kumar. The letter referred to outstanding bills of 26 Kolkata-based pharma suppliers totalling Rs 1 crore.

They were reportedly also carrying a letter related to the procurement of Local Area Network (LAN) testing equipment worth Rs 2,30,048 for the Eastern Command.

"The idea was to sanction the payment on the spot in exchange for 10 per cent of the bill amount. Graft money in cash totalling Rs 5.4 lakh was also recovered from the auditors. Besides these documents, they were also carrying diaries with multiple entries and billing reference numbers. Carrying such documents out of the office seriously compromises the medical and communication security of the forces," sources said.

Heading: Pillion rider not entitled to third-party insurance: SC - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-One people, including five women, died after they drank spurious liquor at Kolar district of Karnataka and Krishnagiri in neighbouring Tamil Nadu, police said on Sunday.

Police said eight persons, including two women, died after consuming spurious liquor in two villages in Kolar on Saturday night. While three persons died in Tekal village where they had consumed it, allegedly distributed by a political party, five others fell victim to the illicit brew in Narasapura, sources said.

People of Narasapura, hearing about the tragedy blocked the Bangalore-Chennai road for some time, demanding immediate closure of an illicit liquor manufacturing unit in their village and arrest of culprits. Police officials rushed to the spot and assured them that action would be taken.

Heading: 16 killed in the third phase of panchayat polls - Indian Express
Content:
A pillion rider who dies or gets injured in a road accident is not entitled to third party insurance claim, the Supreme Court has said. If a vehicle is covered only by a third party insurance, neither the owner, nor the passengers are covered, unless, the contract of insurance is specific that it would cover others too, a Bench of Justices S B Sinha and L S Panta said.

The Bench passed the ruling while quashing the Rs 1.18 lakh compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) in Kerala to the next of a woman pillion rider who died after falling from the scooter on which she was travelling.

The deceased Thankamani was pillion riding a scooter on October 20, 1993 when she accidentally fell down and died. Her family filed a claim for insurance compensation. But Oriental Insurance Company, the insurer, raised a contention that the policy did not cover the risk of injury or death for Thankamani as she was a gratuitous passenger. Hence, it was not liable to pay any compensation for her death.

However, the MACT rejected the insurance company's claim and awarded the Rs 1.18 lakh compensation.

The Kerala High Court later upheld the MACT's decision following which the insurer Oriental Insurance Company filed the appeal in the apex court. Upholding the insurance company's plea, the apex court said that in terms of Section 147 of the Motor Vehicle Act, only in regard to reimbursement of the claim to a third party, a contract of insurance must be taken by the owners of the vehicle.

"The liability of the insurer to reimburse the owner in respect of a claim made by the third party, thus, is statutory whereas other claims are not," the apex court observed. When, however, an owner of a vehicle intends to cover himself from other risks; it is permissible to enter into a contract of insurance in which event the insurer would be bound to reimburse the owner of the vehicle strictly in terms thereof, the Bench said.

The apex court said that the provisions of the MV Act and, in particular, Section 147 were enacted for the purpose of enforcing the principles of social justice.

"It, however, must be kept confined to a third party risk. A contract of insurance that is not statutory in nature should be construed like any other contract," the Bench observed.

In the present case, the bench said, the parties had only entered into a contract of insurance for the purpose of covering the third party risk and not the risk of the owner or a pillion rider.

Heading: China firm to build dam for Mumbai’s water needs - Indian Express
Content:
Violence marred the third phase of panchayat elections in West Bengal with 14 deaths reported from Murshidabad alone where the Congress fought a fierce battle to retain the Murshidabad Zilla Parishad.

Incidentally, the other zilla parishad held by the opposition, out of the 17, is the Malda zilla parishad that is run by the grand alliance of the Congress, Trinamool Congress and BJP.

While in the first phase, held on May 11, no death was reported, in the second phase, held on May 14, seven people died.

On Sunday, polling was held in seven districts — Murshidabad, Malda, Birbhum, Jalpaiguri, North Dinajpur, South Dinajpur and Coochbehar.

Till 3 in the afternoon more than 55 per cent polling was reported from the districts, according to Raj Kanojia, IG, state police. He added that around 100 people were arrested in connection with various violent incidents.

Official sources put the death toll in at 16.

Four deaths were reported from Domkal area of Murshidabad, following clashes between Congress and CPI(M) workers. In Raninagar in Murshidabad district, an altercation between the CPI(M) and Congress workers at a polling station turned violent leading to firing and hurling of bombs.

Congress supporter Bhupati Mondal was shot while a bullet hit a voter. Five others were critically injured in the clash. Mondal later died in the hospital.

In Jalpaiguri district's Madarihat area, the battered body of a CPI(M) supporter was found near National Highway 31.

One person was killed in Birbhum's Nannur district when he was trying to make bombs. But the IG could not confirm these two cases.

The state Election Commission termed the elections peaceful. "The turn-out was low but overall it was peaceful. There were stray incidents and five people lost their lives," S N Roychoudhury, Special Secretary of the Election Commission, said.

CPI(M) state secretary Biman Bose said: "This time the elections have been less violent than that in 2003."

The Congress, on the other hand, expressed hope that it would retain both the Malda and Murshidabad zilla parishads.

"Apart from retaining these two, we will win North Dinajpur zilla parishad too," Subrata Mukherjee, Congress leader, said.

Heading: Seventh time lucky for TN waiter, clears UPSC - Indian Express
Content:
A Chinese state-run firm is all set to become the first from the country to build a dam in India, which aims to ease the drinking water shortage in the country's financial capital Mumbai.

Despite some critics raising the bogey of the security implications of such a project, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has selected a joint venture between China International Water and Electric Engineering (CWE) and India's Soma Enterprises for constructing the Middle Vaitarna dam across the Vaitarna river, about 145 km from Mumbai, sources told The Indian Express.

The civic body selected the company after it submitted a technical bid of Rs 490 crore — well below the projected tender cost of Rs 550 crore. A proposal to approve the selection will be placed before the BMC standing committee of corporators soon, and this is expected to be a mere formality. The project, whose total cost is estimated at Rs 1,600 crore, is one of the most ambitious for the BMC.

When completed in 2011, it aims to supply an additional 450 million litres of water per day. Global tenders were invited last year and seven companies — five of them Chinese — had bid for the project. One Indian and one Chinese firm were disqualified for technical reasons. "We then had to make the selection from the remaining five companies. Since CWE/Soma Enterprises fit all technical aspects of constructing the dam and have also quoted a lower price than the other companies, they have been selected," a top BMC official said. The construction is expected to last three years and use advanced RCC technology, expertise for which was not available for such large projects in India, BMC officials said.

The 105-metre tall dam will be the largest in Maharashtra and will be located in Mokhada in Thane district, almost halfway between Mumbai and Nashik.

But some critics, said to be backed by Indian firms, have launched a campaign through the media against awarding the contracts to Chinese firms, citing what they say are security implications of such a vital project.

They say that the dam, while being a vital installation in itself, will also be located within a few hours from sensitive facilities like the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in Tarapur, defence establishments in Nashik and the currency press there. Besides, in anonymous documents circulated in the media, they have also cited the Central Government's sensitivity over awarding major infrastructure projects to Chinese firms, giving the example of New Delhi directing Chennai and Mumbai port authorities to reject the bid of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Port Holdings to build new container terminals, among others.

But BMC officials dismiss such concerns. They point out that the Chinese firm will only be bringing its technical expertise and its employees would be involved in project management, while the actual construction would be done by Indian labourers.

Security clearances for Chinese nationals would come from New Delhi, they added. "Moreover, there will be security from the civic body at the spot during construction," one official said.

Heading: WB Govt finds molestation charges baseless - Indian Express
Content:
Jayaganesh found his pot of gold just when everyone thought he should resign himself to a life behind the counter of a multiplex snack bar, serving popcorn and cold drinks to crowds of strangers. Four letters meant everything to him: UPSC. They summed up his failures as well as his dreams. In between catering to hungry moviegoers, the civil service hopeful would rush back to his books, devouring each chapter repeatedly. "My job as a waiter started by 10.30 am and went on till 8.30 in the night, but unlike some of my earlier jobs, I had a little more free time. Once the interval rush was over, my colleagues would force me to go back to my lessons," shares the 29-year-old, who secured the 156th rank in the UPSC exammination in his last attempt, after failing to clear it for six consecutive years.

What had begun to seem like a pipe dream began after Jayaganesh completed his degree in mechanical engineering in 2000. Although he joined a small scale industry unit in Bangalore, the job only lasted a year, as the young man believed he had found his true calling: public service. But his first three attempts at clearing the prestigious UPSC exam got him nowhere. "For the first three times, I wrote the test after preparing on my own, sitting in my home in Vinnambalam village in Vellore district. There are no facilities or support there to enable a student to clear something as competitive as this," he says.

Undaunted, Jayaganesh decided to chase his dream to Chennai, 200 kms away from home. At first, there was a glimmer of hope. He cleared the written tests and made it to the interview stage of the examination in his very first attempt in the Tamil Nadu capital. There, he faltered.

"In my fifth attempt, I did not clear the exams. The next time, my sixth, I again reached till the interview stage but failed again. Still, after attending interviews twice, I was confident that I could clear the test if I prepared well," says Jayaganesh.

So, he did. He studied tirelessly, holding down his serving job until the last leg of his preparation period, when he managed to get a teaching position in a private coaching institute. For the final four months, the teacher taught social studies and other general papers to other young hopefuls and prepared himself for the biggest test. He passed it, but the interview remained a challenge.

As he faced the board, he was asked the inevitable questions: Why had he "wasted" eight precious years for this one dream? Was it worth it? He explained the difficulties he had faced in his village, told them how a brief training at the state government-run training institute at Anna Nagar took him till the interview stage in his first year in Chennai.

He made the cut. "Each time I failed, I went back and corrected my mistakes. This was the last possible attempt and I cleared it," says Jayaganesh. Now, he is a celebrity of sorts, welcomed by big floral garlands and fire crackers, flashing cameras and talk shows, and even a PR person for assistance. "I saw the news and decided to help him with his media interviews," said the self-appointed PR agent. Jayaganesh, on the other hand, is still bemused by his new well-wisher. "When a lot of journalists started asking me questions, she arranged a press meet for me to share my experiences. I don't know exactly what her job is," he confesses.

If rags-to-riches is impressive, hardwork and tenacity are inspiring. A few hours after reaching home, he appeared as a guest on a local TV talk show. "During the show, many called in to ask about my preparations and dreams; some asked me doubts from their subjects," said the amused "star", yet to come in terms with his new status.

Jayaganesh is now waiting for August, which is when his training will begin. He looks forward to making his larger dream come true: a dream about villages where there is no violence and where every youngster understands the significance of education and mapping their own future.

"During the interview, they asked me if I was happy. Now I really am."

Jayganesh's Journey

• 2000: Completes engineering degree

• 2001-2003: Fails UPSC written tests three times

• 2004: Reaches interview stage; doesn't pass

• 2005-2007: Fails UPSC twice more

• 2008: Clears UPSC; ranked 156

Heading: Parched land off the IT highway - Indian Express
Content:
The state Government on Sunday gave a clean chit to DIG, CRPF, Alok Raj, against whom a complaint of molestation was lodged at the Nandigram police station on May 11, during the first phase of the panchayat elections. While a complaint of molestation was filed against the CRPF officer, a few CRPF women constables had also filed complaints of molestation and harassment against the local police.

The state Government had appointed Rakesh Gupta, IG, Western Range, to investigate into the complaints. Gupta submitted his report last week.

"No charges of molestation have been proved. In fact, charges of molestation are often lodged against each other (by law enforcement agencies) and it is a dangerous trend. This should be stopped immediately. And another thing, we will have to get along well with everybody," said Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti.

The CRPF DIG expressed his happiness over this clean chit by the state Government.

"I feel happy that I was absolved of the charge. It was filed to frame me. But I knew I was innocent. And now that belief has been vindicated," Aloke Raj said.

Heading: Not welcome, voters tell Dharam Singh - Indian Express
Content:
On the night of January 1, 2008, onion farmer Ramachandra Devendrappa Jainar, 60, struggling under a Rs 9.5 lakh-loan, walked out to his eight-acre land and took his life, in the Byahatti Village of Navalgund Taluk, around 30 km from Hubli City in Karnataka's Dharwad district.

The name of the father of seven girls is now in the list of over 20,000 farmers who have committed suicide in Karnataka over the past decade.

Like many in that list, Ramachandra worked in the hard land of impoverished northern Karnataka that goes to polls in the third phase in the state on May 22.

"I knew he was worried about the loans after our crops failed but he never spoke about it. He got all our daughters married. He would be worrying but I never imagined this," says Ramachandra's 55-year-old wife Kamalavvar. With her daughters married in villages around the northern districts and her husband gone, Kamalavvar now has only the visits of her sons-in-law and daughters to look forward to.

Kamalavvar knows that her family is entitled to some government compensation but has no idea how to get it. The family has not heard of the UPA government's loan waiver scheme, widely promoted by Rahul Gandhi during a visit to the region in March this year and has only a vague idea about a state implemented scheme for families of farmers who commit suicide.

"Some of our local leaders told us to apply for a compensation scheme for farmer suicide families. We don't know how much the compensation will be—something like Rs 1 lakh? We have applied and are hoping something will happen after the election," says her son-in-law, 34-year-old Hanumathappa.

Among the several carrots being dangled before the voting population by political parties —including free colour televisions by the Congress and an almost fully implemented free bicycle scheme by the former JDS-BJP government, what Kamalavvar's family wants is a farm loan interest rate reduction.

The family's borrowings include Rs 5.5 lakh from the Karnataka Vikas Bank at Navalgund and sundry small loans running into Rs 4 lakh.

"He mortgaged our land for the loans. Two days ago, the bank said we will have to pay back the loans to be eligible to borrow again," says Kamalavvar.

Around 30 km away from Byahatti, in the village of Nalavadi in Navalgund taluk, 40-year-old Renuvva, the widow of chilly and onion farmer Nagappa Basappa Siriguppi, 46, killed himself on February 12, 2008, too doesn't know much about compensation schemes.

"We struggled together for 20 years. We could have gone on. He killed himself over a Rs 45,000-loan. What is that amount these days? People who have taken loans for

Rs 2 lakh are living happily around us," says Renuvva, who has now pinned her hopes on her elder son 16-year-old Ravi going to a city like Hubli to fend for the family.

During his school holidays, the 16-year-old has been working as a hired farm labour for wages of Rs 60 per day. "Working the land is a constant process of loss. Every year we borrow and invest for very small returns," says his mother.

However, while cities in the southern parts of Karnataka like Bangalore and Mysore have attracted large investments in sectors like IT, major cities like Hubli in the north have been making slow progress in terms of opportunities. An IT park created in Hubli around five years ago for instance has attracted few big ticket investors and remains largely empty.

Though the issue of regional imbalance is on the political agenda in Karnataka, political parties are yet to address it seriously.

Heading: Another son rise in the hills - Indian Express
Content:
Till recently not many imagined that former Karnataka chief minister Dharam Singh could be dislodged from his Jewarghi constituency in Gulbarga district. After all, he has had eight consecutive wins from here since 1972 and was now looking for a ninth one.

In 2004, Singh won with a margin of just 2,400 votes while in 1999 his margin was 1,950 votes. But the poll battle could be tougher this year.

A few days ago, three villages traditionally loyal to the Congress, didn't even allow Singh to campaign, accusing him of having done little to develop his constituency. Anger against him, a strong farmer leader as rival and a sympathy wave for the BJP, could well topple Singh.

A visit to Balbatti village some 40 km from Gulbarga city throws up signs of things to come. On Sunday, Singh visited Balbatti that has around 2,000 voters, with an extra police escort and a pilot vehicle. The reason: Four days ago, villagers here lined the approach roads with stones and drove Singh away. Similar uprisings were reported in Mardi and Shivpur villages as well.

When he held a sabha in the largest house in the village, most villagers preferred to stay away and chew betel leaves in front of a temple instead. Ramegowda, a farmer from Bulbatti says, "Last time he said he would become CM if we voted for him and he did. But that has not done us any good. We refused to let him enter our village and turned him away." Their village, says Ramegowda, has an acute water shortage and no roads.

Incidentally, in the Nanjundappa committee report, submitted during Veerappa Moily's reign in Karnataka in 1996, Jewarghi was ranked 174 among the 177 backward talukas in the state.

With 2.05 lakh voters of all castes, dominated by Lingayats (Ghaniga), caste is not an important factor in the Jawargi constituency. In Jawargi, there are barely 100 voters from the Rajput community to which Singh belongs. A major reason for Singh's success in the past, say voters, is because his reign is identified as being largely peaceful.

But a deep divide cuts across Singh's birthplace Nilogi, a village with 3,000 voters. In the village, everyone has their own predictions. Rajanna, a local youth believes the Congress at best will manage around 40 per cent of the votes. "Little has been done here except for a couple of RCC roads. The old school where Singh studied, which is the polling station, is in ruins and was fixed up only two days ago for voting," he says.

The fall in Singh's popularity coincides with the rise of his rival, popular farmer leader and independent candidate Kedarlingayya Hirematt.

A man who lead several farmer agitations in the drought-prone Gulbarga, Hirematt lost face in the 1999 assembly elections when he reportedly gave up the poll race on the Congress's request. "I thought I did the right thing 10 years ago but I was wrong. The farmers know what I am capable of and my campaign is running smoothly," says Hirematt.

Meanwhile, in Adrami town, which has about 9,000 voters, the BJP's star campaigner and chief ministerial candidate B.S. Yediurappa holds a public meeting to a packed audience. The BJP candidate against Singh, Dodappa Gowda, is the son of the late Shivlingappa Gowda, who contested against Singh in the last three elections. But Singh doesn't appear to be unduly disturbed by these combined challenges. He visited his constituency for the first time since 2004 only this May and his campaign includes a 10 or 15-minute visit to the 148 villages in Jewarghi. And in Balbatti, Singh chose to speak to TV channels and not villagers.

The voters are now returning the favour.

Heading: Legal hurdles stacked against Indian held in Spain - Indian Express
Content:
In another four days, Hamirpur in Himachal Pradesh will hold a by-election for a Lok Sabha seat, one that Prem Kumar Dhumal won less than a year ago but quit after becoming the state's chief minister in December 2007.

The poll is important for a number of reasons. This is Dhumal's first popularity test after he led the BJP to a spectacular victory last year. Dhumal's hold over Hamirpur — a mid-hill district — has strengthened over the years. The constituency that extends over the districts of Bilaspur, Una, Hamirpur and Kangra, had been a Congress bastion till Dhumal started nurturing this ex-servicemen- and farmer-dominated belt. It's due to his efforts that Hamirpur switched its loyalty from the Congress to the BJP.

But this time the battle in Hamirpur is a bit different. This year, Dhumal's son Anurag Thakur, 34, has jumped into the election fray, contesting from Hamirpur on a BJP ticket. For Dhumal, it's important that not only his son win, but that he also maintains his winning margin. In the previous election, Dhumal had won this seat by a record 80,000 votes, turning around the fortunes of the BJP in Himachal. His victory was a big blow to the Congress, which lost the 2007 Assembly elections.

This is the second by-election in Hamirpur in two years. Last year the seat fell vacant after BJP MP Suresh Chandel was expelled along with nine other MPs in the cash-for-query scam. Anurag Thakur could have become the BJP's candidate then but neither Dhumal nor the party was willing to take any risk in an Assembly election year. If Thakur wins now, Dhumal would have secured this seat for the future and would have successfully launched his son.

But for Dhumal, the larger challenge lies in consolidating the gains and in keeping his detractors at bay before the state goes to the Lok Sabha polls in 2009. Of Himachal's four Lok Sabha seats, three are with the Congress at present.

Many in the BJP have accused Dhumal of promoting parivarvad (family rule) but the criticisms don't appear to have had any adverse effect on his son's political prospects.

Thakur—who also heads the Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association—-a post he occupied when Dhumal became chief minister in 1998, is quite popular with the state's youth. He is also credited with building an international cricket stadium at Dharamshala. In fact, he single-handedly fought a protracted legal battle against the Congress government's attempt to remove him as the state cricket body chief.

"I got the ticket to the Lok Sabha on my merit. In fact it's cricket, not my father that got me the BJP candidature. I will try to do my best and prove that the party was not wrong in giving the youth a chance by choosing me," he says.

Apart from his popularity, what also works in Thakur's favour is a fractured Opposition. The Congress, after losing the Assembly elections, has not made much of an effort to regroup and reach out to the people. The BJP, on the other hand, has managed to bury its differences and rally behind Dhumal and his son.

Heading: Black Widow strikes terror - Indian Express
Content:
While Roshan Jamal Khan has been under arrest in Spain for nearly four months now, charges are yet to be framed against him in court. And the law under which he is serving pre-trial detention could keep him behind bars for even up to two years. Khan is the lone Indian who is accused by the Spanish authorities of being part of an Al Qaeda cell, planning a terror attack.

So far, Khan has been brought to court only once in January to be ordered into "unconditional" pre-trial detention, says his brother-in-law, Amanullah Khan who stays in Spain. "We are now waiting to file a plea for his release," Amanullah told The Indian Express on the telephone from Spain, adding it was going to be an uphill task.

Khan is facing pre-trial detention under Section 503 of the Spanish Criminal Procedure Act (LECrim) which can be ordered if the crime a person is accused of is punishable by a maximum prison sentence of two years or even less than that in case of a criminal record. Still, other clauses under the section strengthen the case for a pre-trial detention if the accused presents a "risk of flight" from the country or if there is danger he may try to conceal/alter/destroy sources of evidence.

The fact that Khan is also accused of having overstayed his visa could further work against him, though his family claims he had applied for a residence permit along with his brother-in law Amanullah and the local police had allowed him to stay until a final decision on his permit application was taken.

Things look quite bleak for Khan as legal experts on Spanish law say the persons accused of serious crimes — those involving a prison sentence of more than three years — may be kept in detention for up to four years as well and in terrorism cases, detention up to two years is not unusual. While Article 528 under LECrim does allow "provisional liberty", the fact is that under Article 503, which Khan is facing, if there is "reasonable enough" prima facie evidence suggesting criminal responsibility of the accused, the detention will stay. When Khan was arrested along with nine others from a mosque, the cops claimed to have recovered nitrocellulose and some other explosives from the mosque and presented this as evidence in court.

Though the Indian embassy in Spain has been communicating with the Interior Ministry of Spain on the issue asking for more clarity on the charges against him, there has been practically no light of hope for Roshan. As he mostly speaks Urdu, the language barrier is posing a great difficulty for him and his family, who had to get the Spanish detention orders translated into English. He has been telling his wife Farida in Mumbai on the phone that he was made to sign Spanish documents he did not understand.

Though Khan's family in India has approached everyone from the Prime Minister to the Leader of the Opposition, no help has come their way. A distraught Mehboob Khan, brother of Roshan, has now knocked on the doors of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and Amnesty International.

"I had filed a complaint with both NHRC and Amnesty two-three months ago but did not get any response. So I came to Delhi to check with them.
