A highly placed official said, "Implementation of this project would reduce the time taken to evacuate storm water, improve drainage and enable reclaiming of waterlogged areas. However, these measures won't last long if no corrections are made at the source of seepage, namely the Rajasthan and Sirhind feeder canals."

The proposal, therefore, also calls for a project to reline sections of these two canals, the estimated cost of which would be Rs 425 crore for the Rajasthan canal and Rs 225 crore for the Sirhind canal.

Apart from reducing the waterlogging problem, this will save a lot of water for Punjab. Akali Dal president Sukhbir Badal admitted to The Indian Express that seepages in the canals lead to a 30 per cent loss of the total water purveyed through them. The water saved as a result of this project will irrigate about 2 lakh acres of land in Rajasthan and Punjab, and it is estimated that it could increase the agriculture production in two states to the tune of Rs 300 crore per annum.

The state government has requested the Centre for Rs 650 crore as special grant for relining and Rs 300 crore as a one-time grant to implement the anti-waterlogging project.

In deep waters

• Close to 8,4,800 hectares of land in Muktsar, Faridkot and Ferozepur districts are "critically waterlogged" according to government sources, making them unfit for cultivation. Around 35 per cent of the total area's population has been affected.

• Water seepage from canals is a continuing problem. Although dependence on them has decreased over the years, 27 per cent of the arable land in the state is still irrigated by canals.

• The problem is exacerbated because the groundwater in these areas is too saline to be suitable for irrigation.

Heading: As parties do some quick math, all eyes on Gowda - Indian Express
Content:
The SGPC on Friday decided to grant Rs 1 lakh each to the kin of soldiers killed in transit during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The decision was taken at a meeting of the SGPC Executive under the chairmanship of SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar. A committee has been formed to verify the claims of such soldiers.

Makkar said though the exact number of such soldiers was not known, a list of 50 has been provided by Col Pratap Singh Phulka. The soldiers' familes will be paid relief after verification of their cases.

Though coming after almost 24 years of their death, the relief was welcomed by Col Phulka, secretary general of the ex-servicemen wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal, who has been collecting data in this regard for the past six years. "It will be some help to the poor kin, though a bit late," he said. "It had became my mission to identify such soldiers after I retired in 2002. These soldiers had been totally forgotten by all governments."

Though the exact number of such deaths is uncertain, Col Phulka has a record of 50 such soldiers who died in anti-Sikh riots in various cities, while they were in transit.

Earlier, SGPC had provided compensation to soldiers who had deserted the Army in the wake of Operation Bluestar. Such suldiers were given the status of 'Dharmi Faujis" and provided Rs 50,000 each.

Heading: The stakes are high - Indian Express
Content:
With less than 48 hours left for the Karnataka Assembly election results to be declared, both the Congress and the BJP curiously agree that their party's fate is dependent on the performance of Deve Gowda's JD(S) and the continued Vokkaliga support.

The Congress is keen to see the decimation of Gowda's party so that it is in direct contest with the BJP, but the saffron party does not want the JD(S) to shed too many seats from the 58 that it previously held in the Vidhan Soudha.

While the Congress leadership is not very upbeat about the Karnataka Assembly results, it is banking on the Siddaramiah (Kurba)-M.P. Prakash (Lingayat)-C.M. Ibrahim (minorities) vote-bank along with Mallikarjun Kharge's Dalit support base, S.M. Krishna's urban reach and Vokkaliga base to deliver the goods. The Congress's Karnataka managers, however, still feel that they could have done slightly better if the high command had not insisted on giving 17 tickets to minorities, 11 tickets to women and two tickets to Christians. The fact is that the Congress had to drop two sitting MLAs from Dharwad and North Belgaum to accommodate minority candidates and women seats had to be increased from the previous seven to 11 even when there weren't enough women candidates. One of the two dropped candidates later turned rebel and is now in a winning position.

The BJP, on its part, is confident of emerging at least as the single largest party after being helped by the 7.8 per cent inflation, and the Hubli and Jaipur bomb blasts. However, the party's election managers are banking on the BSP increasing its vote share from three to five per cent and the JD(S) vote share going down only marginally from the previous 20 to 17 per cent to split the Vokkaliga vote. The fact is that in the previous Assembly, the BJP had captured 79 seats with a vote share of only 28 per cent and the Congress managed only 65 seats with a larger vote share of 35 per cent. The saffron party's only fear is of a Vokkaliga consolidation as BJP's chief ministerial candidate B.S. Yeddyurappa belongs to the Lingayat community.

But the leaders of the two main parties feel that the Assembly elections would be decided on the money spent by each candidate as the Election Commission had imposed severe restrictions on open campaigning. The official figure of money seized by the Commission is some Rs 60 crore besides the urban land, educational, sugar, arrack and iron ore mafias playing their part in the process.

While the central Congress leadership believes that a fair candidate selection will see them through, it is also banking on the BJP's electoral fortunes being hit with Bangarappa joining the SP and the JD(U) fighting the election independently. However, the Congress knows that S.M. Krishna's magic has not worked with the urban electorate. Siddaramiah's open claim for the Congress CM slot and Janardhan Poojary's promise of revoking the ban on arrack haven't helped matters either. The party is banking on Kharge's electoral reach with the dalits and feels that BSP's P.G.R. Scindia will not be able to make a mark on the Karnataka scene at least this time.

However, there is much anxiety in the Capital with the post-poll scenario if a hung assembly result is thrown up on May 25. A section within the Congress feels that the party should allow the BJP, if it emerges as the single largest party, to tie-up with the JD(S) and form the government as this arrangement would not last. The counter view is that BJP should not be allowed to form its first government in the south as it would be a continuation of the saffron party's recent victories in Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh and would set the tone for the general elections.

Heading: ‘Pakistan is constantly relearning how to be a democracy’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Karnataka assembly elections are finally over and the verdict is sealed in the electronic voting machines. The strict enforcement of the model code of conduct by the Election Commission has been welcomed by one and all but it could still not fully prevent the blatant use of money power, especially in Central Karnataka, where the mining lobbies were in full operation. The bomb blasts at Hubli and Jaipur also created a flutter.

The people of Karnataka are eagerly looking towards an integrated and holistic approach to planning for sustained development, combining environmental, economic, cultural and social aspects along with political stability. IT has become the heart and soul of Karnataka, especially Bangalore and Mysore. Any government that takes over must take forward the IT revolution that was started by the Congress in 1976, with the Electronic City Initiative, followed by the International Technology Park in 1993 and the e-governance initiatives in 2000.

However, the problems associated with rapid urbanisation in Bangalore has led to a number of social and economic problems, including poverty, hunger, homelessness, crime, and diseases.

The citizens of Bangalore keenly await the formation of a new government which will address the important issue of an independent regulatory authority for the real estate sector, property tax reforms and repeal of the capital value based system. Traffic is also a key issue in Bangalore and every citizen wants the new government to come out with a comprehensive Integrated Traffic Management Plan for the city. Now that the new airport at Devanahalli has become operational, high speed connectivity will be the prime concern for the incoming government.

The implementation of the Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee's recommendations for addressing the regional imbalance in growth, especially between North and South Karnataka, is a very important issue, which all political parties have promised to address on top priority, if voted to power.

There are high stakes for some political parties in the Karnataka assembly elections. Though the BJP emerged as the single largest party in 2004, the outcome of the assembly elections will decide whether or not it has gained the acceptance of the people of Karnataka. For the BJP, the results of the Karnataka elections will give an indication of the mood of voters in the run-up to the Lok Sabha elections. The BJP's performance in Karnataka will decide if it can continue to rely on emotive themes such as Hindu nationalism or bank on real issues related to governance and economic development.

The elections will also test both the JD(S) and the BSP. The credibility of the JD(S) as a political party and especially the acceptability of Deve Gowda and his flip-flop politics will be either established or exposed. Similarly, the BSP, which is trying to project itself as a national party, needs to make convincing gains in a sizable number of constituencies and vote share to sustain their tall claims.

The fiasco played out by the JD(S) and the BJP recently has made people wary of these two parties in the state. They traded charges of opportunistic politics and treason, blaming each other for the fall of the government. This has helped the Congress, which, throughout the election campaign, projected positive factors and fought the elections on the plank of development, stability and inclusive growth with balanced regional development. Although price rise was an issue, the Congress was able to convince people, that this was linked to the international economic situation and inflation would be under control in next couple of months. Of course, only the election results will show whether people have accepted the explanation offered by Congress.

Though poll surveys have predicted a hung assembly, it is my view that the reality may turn out to be completely different and a surprise at that.

Veerappa Moily is a former Karnataka chief minister and a senior Congress leader

Heading: She set the stage for Cong’s good show - Indian Express
Content:
•Pakistan's history has been cyclical: an instalment of military rule followed by a civilian interregnum and then another instalment of military rule. Even during civilian rule, the army is omnipresent. Why is this, and how does it thwart Pakistan's quest for nationhood?

Pakistan, unlike India, failed to develop a sustainable democratic polity. The army has traditionally been a powerful and respected institution. Not only does the army tend to interfere in civil administration and usurp power, but weak civilian leaders also tend to involve the army in political battles and then regret doing so. Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Benazir, Nawaz Sharif — have all paid the price for this folly. Bhutto's first mistake was to promote the reclusive Zia-ul-Haq, who kept his thoughts to himself, and then, more importantly, to invite him to the cabinet meetings. Those meetings exposed the weakness of Bhutto's colleagues and Zia decided that that house of cards had to go. On the whole, the army has always been Pakistan's most powerful and visible institution. It has done well to protect the country's borders. It will remain powerful and any emerging system has to take it on board. But Pakistan needs to draw a clear line between the civil and the military. Pakistan is constantly relearning how to be a democracy.

•Aren't the amendments to the Warrant of Precedence a reflection of Pakistan's history? Incidentally, Nawaz Sharif learnt about the Warrant from you?

Yes. The Warrant of Precedence was a colonial legacy and spelt out the relative ranking of civil and military officials for protocol. In the WOP issued in 1950, the army chief was much lower down the order at number 15. Pakistan has periodically amended the WOP to elevate the military posts...Sharif was complaining about the army invading every civilian political space. So I had asked him if he was aware of the WOP. He wasn't. But then he remembered how, on a visit to Dhaka on Khaleda Zia's invitation, he found the army chief way down the line. I told him that Bangladesh had reverted to the 1950 WOP. The WOP is not important in itself. But it helps maintain the relative rankings. Nevertheless, Pakistan 's civilian leaders in recent times never tried to change the amended WOP.

•Your book studies the corporate structure and identity of the Pakistan army.

The army is a corporate entity in the sense that it indulges in self-aggrandisement...business, subsidised state assets, estates. This is the result of military and quasi-military rule and also of the tendency of civilian leaders to placate the army, either as bribes or "in appreciation" of the work they do. The army thus sticks together, protecting its interests. It even acts against its own leadership whenever the latter compromises the army's image or power—thus were Ayub Khan and Yahya Khan removed.

About Islamists in the army...most of the military is in the middle ground. Despite Zia's Islamisation drive, in my conversations with officers, I haven't detected the kind of militancy that outsiders, particularly the West, fear. In fact, the Institute of Strategic Studies has called Pakistan's nuclear safeguards "robust". Most officers, even the Zia recruits, shun civilian administration. Today, they'd much rather there were a competent civilian government.

•You are a critic of US policy towards Pakistan.

There have been big advantages of the relationship. Both the economy and the military have benefited from it. But increasing Pakistani vulnerability and US sanctions weakened the country. The so-called Zia recruits will be filling the top posts of the army when the present batch retires. But they were deprived of the opportunity to go to the US for training because of sanctions. Stability in Pakistan requires US investment in the economy as well as the army. But the aid that is offered is less than what is promised. The relationship suffers from a temporal disconnect. The US cannot focus on long-term policy. It seeks tactical alliances to solve its immediate problems. It did so during the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and again in 2001. The fear in Pakistan is that the US will move out of Afghanistan again, leaving Pakistan with very angry populations on both sides of the Durand Line.

•You have a chapter dealing with the structural reforms you suggest in the army.

The recruitment of the Pakistan army is more representative of Pakistani society today. The homogeneity of the army is passé. However, the top brass is still inducted on the basis of a highly personalised selection, thus promoting sycophants and clones of the COAS. Pakistan needs integrated regional commands and a smaller, lighter force with greater mobility.

Greater power to regional commanders would eliminate the all-powerful nature of the COAS, reducing thereby the chances of a coup. To build a viable political system, the army has to subject itself to control, submitting before Parliament, and the civilian government has to stop involving the army in political disputes.

Heading: Navy readied ship to take on pirates - Indian Express
Content:
The expanse of a stage can sometimes bring the best out of people. Like it did for Dipa Das Munshi, wife of Union I&B Minister Priya Ranjan Das Munshi. Once an established theatre actress, Dipa stepped on to the political stage and is now being hailed as the newest star of the West Bengal Congress, the architect of the party's win in the panchayat election in Uttar Dinajpur.

Today, as the CPI(M) reels under an unimpressive show in the rural elections, she can claim to have played a part in scripting the CPI(M)'s misfortunes. As Dipa campaigned for the Congress, she knew this was just another part she played to perfection. "Both theatre and politics are people oriented. Both require a stage. It's only from the stage that one can interact with the masses," she said.

Dipa began her rise in West Bengal politics by defeating Hafiz Alam Sairani, a firebrand minister in the Left Front government, in the 2006 Assembly elections from Goalpokhor constituency in Uttar Dinajpur.

While campaigning around the districts in the run-up to the panchayat polls, Dipa would be impeccably dressed in brightly coloured cotton saris and team them with a huge bindi and danglers. She would walk straight into the backyard of the homes she visited and chat with the women of the household. The people of North Dinajpur were more than happy to vote for their 'Boudi' (elder brother's wife).

"I might appear urbane and city-bred but at the same time, I can relate extremely well with the rural masses. Being the wife of the I&B minister and PCC president has its advantages. Local leaders confide in me and tell me things they cannot tell the PCC president. Moreover, being Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi's wife gives me an added identity. The disadvantage is that my movement gets restricted for security reasons," she joked.

For the first time in 2008, Dipa was able to bring unity into the district Congress that was torn apart by various factions.

Dipa is said to know all the party workers by their names and holds informal meetings and discussions with each one of them.

After the victory of the district Congress in North Dinajpur, party sources say Dipa could be the next Sabhadipati of the Zilla parishad.

Heading: UP polio strain found in Angola - Indian Express
Content:
Just before the Indian sailors onboard hijacked ship MV Victoria were released on Friday, India had readied a frontline guided missile destroyer, complete with a crack marine commandos (MARCOS) team, for a rescue mission to the Somalia coast.

The strike mission was called off after the issue got resolved, but it has come to light that the Navy had prepared for any extreme eventuality and readied one its most modern warships, the guided missile destroyer INS Delhi, for a fast dash to the Somali coast.

A crack team of the Navy's elite anti-terror special operations unit, which is trained for operations on oil rigs and merchant ships, was placed on board the INS Delhi on Thursday morning.

Officers and sailors of the warship who had gone on leave were called back on 'emergency duty' for the mission.

Sources confirmed that the heavily armed warship, which carries two Sea King helicopters and reaches speeds greater thab 32 knots, was hours away from deployment when the situation deescalated.

However, the INS Mumbai, another Delhi class destroyer, was asked to head to Somalia to keep track of the hijacked ship. INS Mumbai was already in African waters as it was returning from an exercise with the South Africa and Brazil navies, although it did not have a MARCOS team onboard

While a rescue mission to Somalia would have required an approval from the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS), the incident shows that the Navy was prepared to launch what would have been its first ever strike operation at such a distance from Indian waters.

Besides the IPKF operations in Sri Lanka between 1987-1990, the only other time MARCOS operated beyond Indian waters was near Maldives during Operation Cactus in 1988.

Heading: No law to prosecute Jogi in cash-for-MLA scam, says CBI - Indian Express
Content:
India is again being blamed for the export of a polio virus: a P-3 polio case in Angola, in south-central Africa, is being linked to Uttar Pradesh, which has the second largest number of polio cases in India.

In 2008 Angola has reported five polio cases, one of type-1 and the rest type-3. The May report of WHO's Global Polio Eradication Programme says: "This is the first importation of type 3 poliovirus into Angola and genetic sequencing indicates that the first type 3 case detected (with onset of paralysis on 19 March) is related to the virus from UP, India."

Not only this, the report also observes: "The type 3 polio virus detected in Angola (a new importation from India) underlines the ongoing risk that endemic countries pose to the rest of the world."

Earlier, in 2005, type 1 polio virus strains found in western UPwere traced in Angola and Congo. Then, type 1 virus was considered more dangerous as it spreads in a wider area.

However, with the finding of type-3 polio virus of UP's strain in Angola, a question has been raised over the intensity of P3 virus as well. It is to be noted that to this date, India has reported 225 P-3 cases, out which 172 are from Bihar and 48 are from Uttar Pradesh. While Bihar has reported one P-1 virus, no P-1 has been reported in UP so far.

Talking to The Indian Express, Dr Rajendra Kumar, Director General, Medical and Health, UP Government, said, "We have not got any such reports of fresh importation of polio virus from UP to any other part of the world but if it is P-3, then we are not surprised because this year we have had just one round of P3 vaccination. However, we still believe that P-3 can be controlled easily and a few more rounds of P-3 vaccination in UP would mean elimination of the virus from the state."

In Angola, all cases of polio have been reported from the capital Luanda. While the country had conducted a monovalent PV1 drive in April mid, it conducted mixed OPV1 and PV3 drive recently in the month of May. Angola remained free from polio since September 2001 until 2005 when 11 polio cases were reported. In 2007, the number went up to 13.

Heading: Hizb chief asks Pakistan Govt to stop ‘Junoon’ from performing in Srinagar - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly five years after registering a case against former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Ajit Jogi in cash-for-MLA scam, the CBI now says he cannot be prosecuted under any law. The CBI, in a note conveyed to the Law Ministry, has said that there is no provision either under the Indian Penal Code or Prevention of Corruption Act under which the Congress MP could be prosecuted, Law Ministry sources said.

On December nine, 2003, the CBI registered a case under Prevention of Corruption Act against Jogi, his son Amit and defected BJP MP P R Khunte for allegedly trying to bribe BJP MLAs after the Assembly elections in the state. Jogi is alleged to have bribed BJP leaders to prevent the saffron party from forming the Government in the state after the Assembly polls.

However, after scrutinising statements of Jogi and available provisions under the law, the investigating agency came to the conclusion that no case can be registered against him in the scam as he was the "caretaker" chief minister at the time of the alleged crime and he, therefore, could not come under the category of public servant, the sources said.

The ball is now in the Law Ministry's court which would have to take a decision. Interestingly, the CBI is silent whether the case should be closed against Jogi.

The CBI had registered a case against the three also under section 34 of IPC, which states that "when a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for the act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone".

The FIR also cites section 120-B (criminal conspiracy) against all three of them besides some sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act. As per the opinion of the CBI, a case could not be registered against Jogi either under Prevention of Corruption Act, Representation of the People's Act or the Indian Penal Code, the sources said.

The turn of event took place after the investigating agency mulled how to prosecute Jogi and others despite the voice spectrographic test confirming that Jogi had spoken to the BJP MLAs and offered Rs 25 lakh to prevent the party from forming the Government in the state.

Heading: HC clears way for new Bangalore airport - Indian Express
Content:
Hizbul Mujahideen (HM) chief Syed Salahuddin has urged the Pakistan Government not to allow rock group Junoon to perform in Srinagar on May 25. Salahuddin has said the performance will have a negative impact on the "disputed status" of Kashmir and will send a wrong signal to the international community that "Kashmir was an integral part of India".

"Pakistan should not let any of its cultural groups, such as Junoon, to perform in the disputed territory of Kashmir where any national or international activity amounts to open violation of international laws," said Salahuddin in a statement.

"The performance by a Pakistani singing group will send a wrong message to Kashmiris and give India an opportunity to reaffirm that Kashmir is its integral part," he said. Salahuddin also urged the Pakistan Government to stop India from holding any other international or regional event in Kashmir. "Pakistan should hold back Junoon. Seeing Pakistani boys and girls singing and dancing on stage in Kashmir would dash the expectations of Kashmiris," he said.

Junoon, a Pakistani sufi-pop band is scheduled to perform in Srinagar next Sunday. For the first time, any Pakistani music band will perform in Kashmir. Junoon's show will take place on the banks of the Dal lake for an audience of over 10,000 people, including President Pratibha Patil.

Besides, Union Minister Mani Shankar Aiyar, Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad and Governor S K Sinha are also expected to attend the programme.

Junoon is coming to Kashmir on the South Asia Foundation's (SAF) invitation. SAF Director of Operations Karan Khosla told The Himalayan Mail that the Foundation has also sponsored the Kashmir Study Institute at the Kashmir University (KU), to be inaugurated by President Patil.

Heading: Antony to visit Berlin War Cemetery during Germany trip - Indian Express
Content:
Ending suspense on the opening of the new Bangalore International Airport, the Karnataka High Court late on Friday evening refused to stay the closure of the existing HAL airport and cleared the path for the first flight to take off from the new airport at 12:10 am on Saturday.

Two separate groups of citizens including Bangalore Connect — an organisation comprising several business heads and citizens groups — had moved the High Court, seeking a stay on the May 16 order for closure of the HAL airport issued by the Civil Aviation Ministry.

The petitioners claimed the Central and state governments had failed to conduct a due process of renegotiation with the Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) for keeping the HAL airport open — as suggested by a division Bench of the High Court on April 16 in the course of an interim order in a batch of PILs.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation, however, produced minutes of two meetings held on April 29 and May 23 with BIAL to consider the issue of keeping the HAL airport open for short haul flights and small aircraft.

During the course of the hearing of the applications filed before the vacation Bench, BIAL stated that it was not averse to further renegotiation while the Civil Aviation Ministry said that it would need about 12 weeks' time to assess ground realities and complete renegotiations.

Following the general consensus on a rethink about the HAL airport, the Bench comprising Justice Ram

Mohan Reddy and Justice Javid Rahim stated that it was not inclined to accept the claim for staying closure of the old airport.

The court, however, severely criticised the Union Government and the Karnataka Government for failing to apprehend connectivity problems to the new airport when the commercial agreements were signed for its creation.

"It was incumbent on the state and Central government to take measures to ease traffic flow to the new airport at an early stage," the Bench observed. The airport was first scheduled to open on March 30 but the date was postponed to May 11 on the directions of the Civil Aviation Ministry.

Subsequently, it was postponed to May 23 on account of Karnataka Assembly elections between May 10 and May 22. The opening on May 23 was again pushed to May 24 on the directions of the Election Commission.

Heading: Scientists form body to oppose Pay panel recommendations, demand better deal - Indian Express
Content:
Defence Minister AK Antony, who is heading for a three-day visit to Germany on Sunday, will visit the Berlin War Cemetery to pay his respects to the graves of 51 Indian soldiers who died during the IInd World War.

Antony, who will also attend the Berlin Air Show and hold talks with his German counterpart Dr Franz Josef Jung, will start off official engagements with a visit to the cemetery that has over 3,600 commonwealth graves. A majority of the Indian graves belong to airmen who lost their lives in air raids over Berlin and parts of Eastern Germany. The remaining are of soldiers who died in prisoner of war (POW) camps of Poland and Eastern Germany.

The minister will accompany German Chancellor Angela Merkel at a mega event too that will mark the opening of the Air Show on May 27. India is for the first time participating in this air show as a partner country.

A separate India pavilion, covering 1,200 sq meters, will have displays from several defence public sector undertakings including the likes of Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI), the Ordinance Factory Board (OFB), the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Major private sector defence industries including TATA, Larsen & Toubro and CADES are also participating.

The Sarang helicopter aerobatic team of IAF will also perform during the air show.

Heading: Friends celebrate Aarushi’s life on website - Indian Express
Content:
A group of scientists belonging to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space on friday said the revisions announced by the Sixth Pay Commission have fallen short of their expectations. To add insult to injury, their compatriots in the teaching line and bureaucracy have galloped past them in terms of gross monthly pay, they claimed, adding that this results in huge variations between the salaries between different professionals as they go up the hierarchy.

"While a babu can reach the highest tier, Pay Band IV, within 15 years of service, a scientist would have earned only two promotions after joining as a scientific officer," said S Joseph Winston, a senior scientist at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Kalpakkam.

Their growing discontent has prompted a group of scientists to band together to form the Confederation of Atomic and Space Scientists/Technologists (COAST), an umbrella organisation that has vowed to take up the issue to the higher authorities.

Both the departments come under the Prime Minister who had earlier assured the scientists of a hike of40 per cent.

However, the actual revision has only been around 18 to 35 per cent, complained the scientists, adding that the highest hike was limited to the PB IV category.

"While about 50-60 per cent of the bureaucrats fall in the PB IV, the figure for us scientists is only 5 per cent. Most scientists slog in the labs for years together, and retire before they can ever reach the highest pay structure," said Winston, the president of COAST.

This disparity, said Winston and his colleagues, was a blow to the morale of the scientists who were working on projects of great strategic importance and symbolic value. "There are big investments in the fields of nuclear and space research. It is in these scientific fields where the country proved its might. But when it comes to managing human resources, these shortcomings could have serious consequences. If this situation continues, the country will face a dearth of serious researchers and scientists in the near future," warned Winston, who believes that the Sixth Pay Commission is precisely the sort of policy that causes "brain drain" from premier institutes.

"When there are avenues for them to go abroad and earn manifold of what the Government is offering, none of the 'creamy layer' from institutions like the IITs would come forward to join service here," said a scientist.

Heading: Now, a hooch tragedy in Hassan - Indian Express
Content:
Aarushi had scrawled a message on the 'wall' of her Facebook site the day before she died: "My birthday is coming, please wish me!" unveils a community formed on an Internet social networking site by some of her classmates. The name of the community is "RIP (Rest In Peace) Aarushi," and has already garnered as many as 432 posts commemorating the girl who was found murdered in her house on May 16. On Friday, the father of the class IX student was arrested for the crime, but Aarushi's friends want to remember her life, not just the terrible way she died.

"Her presence lightened the atmosphere in the IX wing, even though she never opened her mouth very often. She was loved by all and there were many things we wanted to say but she went," says the first note on the memorial site.

In the real world, Aarushi's friends celebrated her birthday by lighting candles on her empty desk, but memories of how vibrant she was kept pouring into the virtual club: her friends remembered how much she used to enjoy performing Ashley Lobo steps in the school corridors, how keen she was to be a part of her school's prestigious Interact Club, how she looked forward to joining taekwondo classes. The write-up described Aarushi's serious side as well: juniors looked up to her, she was captain of the 'Ganges House', she once prepared a meaningful project on drug abuse.

We also learn how those who loved Aarushi were devastated by the crime — her best friend (name withheld) was numb after losing her and was almost mute with shock after the incident. Providing a touching glimpse into the complexities of teenage life, the site reveals how two boys were in love with her; one who could not express his feelings when Aarushi was alive and the other who became one of her closest friends.

Calling it "ironic," the post revealed that while playing a game with her friends a few days before, Aarushi had told them "I will be always be there for all of you, whether I am physically present or not. Love you all."

Her friends can only hope she can see their answer on the website: "We love you and you will always be in our hearts no matter where you are."

Heading: EC notices to two Andhra ministers - Indian Express
Content:
In a fresh hooch tragedy in Karnataka, four persons died and 15 others were hospitalised after drinking the brew during a marriage function at Holalaholli village in the district on Friday. With this, the toll in the series of hooch tragedies that has struck parts of Karnataka and neighbouring Tamil Nadu since Sunday climbed to 174.

The incident occurred at the village where the illicit liquor was served after a wedding. Soon after consuming the brew, 19 persons developed complications and four of them died.

Fifteen persons were under treatment in a Hassan hospital and the condition of some of them was stated to be critical.

The police have arrested liquor vendor Mahesh, who supplied the brew.

Meanwhile, Karnataka Police on Friday said six more persons allegedly involved in supply of illicit liquor had been arrested.

While three main suppliers of the killer brew, Syed Asghar, Syed Kadir and Imtiaz, all natives of Bailanarasapura, the place where the brew was manufactured, were arrested in Kolar district on Friday, three vendors of the brew were arrested in Bangalore Rural district on Friday.

Heading: Rains over, prepare for a sweaty May-end - Indian Express
Content:
Andhra Pradesh Home Minister K Jana Reddy and Irrigation Minister P Lakshmaiah have been served notices by the Election Commission for alleged violation of model code of conduct ahead of the May 29 bypolls in the state.

Taking note of a complaint by the Opposition TDP, the poll panel asked Reddy and Lakshmaiah to submit their replies by May 24. The allegation against the ministers was that they had participated in an election meeting held on the premises of a government school at Junevada village in Warangal district where by-elections are to be held. As per the code of conduct, conducting campaign rallies on government premises is not allowed. "I have never violated election code in my entire political career. I am ready to face any action if the EC feels that I have flouted any norms," Reddy said.

The model code of conduct is in force in 10 districts, where by-elections to four Lok Sabha and 18 Assembly constituencies are scheduled to be held on May 29.

Heading: Civilian casualties in Assam have gone up in last four years: MHA report - Indian Express
Content:
Prolonged rains and thunderstorms that had cooled Delhi and northwest India in the last few days are not likely to continue any longer and temperatures are expected to soar again by next week. But the good news is that the forecast for a normal monsoon remains unaffected.

This month has received about 120 mm of rains till now which is significantly higher than the last ten year's average for May of about 42 mm. On Friday, weather scientists said that while isolated rains and thunder showers were still possible in the next one or two days, continuous rains of the sort witnessed over the last week were highly unlikely.

A combination of three wind systems that had formed over northwest India was responsible for the rains. These systems were now disintegrating and therefore rainfall would no longer continue, a weather expert pointed out. He said there was no fear of these systems interfering with the southwest monsoon scheduled to arrive on the Kerala coast on its normal date of June 1.

"There is still some time for the onset of monsoon in Kerala. The wind systems prevailing over northwest India for the last few days could have affected the monsoon only if they had persisted till the onset of monsoon. But these systems are disintegrating rapidly and the formation of monsoon system is also normal," he said. "From Sunday, there is a strong likelihood of intense heat in northern and northwestern India which is normal in this season," he warned.

The all-time record for maximum rains in this month was registered in 2002 May, which had seen 129.3 mm of rains in Delhi. That was also a year of failed monsoon. But experts were quick to point out that there was no direct correlation between the two events.

"There have been years when we had good rains in May followed by a good monsoon and low rainfall in May followed by bad monsoon," a senior official of the Indian Meteorological Department said. Data for the last ten years corroborate his view. Last year, which had witnessed a good monsoon, there was 71.5 mm rain in May, much above average. Similarly, in 2004, May got only 37.7 mm of rainfall but it was a year of bad monsoon.

With the harvesting of rabi season over, there was no danger of any adverse effect on the crops because of these rains. In fact, it was likely to be beneficial for sugarcane, the only major standing crop, as also vegetables and fruits. However, there was a possibility of some fruits falling before getting ripe because of the thunderstorms. Farmers who might have opted for an early sowing of some crops like cotton also might have to go for re-sowing, a weather scientist said.

Heading: Now, corporate sector eyes services of ex-servicemen - Indian Express
Content:
Violent incidents have shown an upward trend in Assam in the past three-four years, with the number of civilian casualties also going up sharply, says the latest annual report of the Home Ministry.

The report says while there were 267 violent incidents in the state during 2004, the number had gone up to 474 in 2007. Likewise, the number of civilians who lost their lives in violent incidents went up from 194 in 2004 to 287 last year.

"The security situation in Assam (and Manipur) continued to be a matter of concern. In Assam, after a lull, following the suspension of operations against the ULFA in 2006 in the context of talks with them, which was apparently utilised by them for consolidation and reorganisation of their cadres, there was an increase in violence, particularly in areas of Upper Assam and Guwahati city," the report says.

Interestingly, while ULFA-related violence has been slightly lower in the current year, Assam has been witnessing a never-before law and order situation in the North Cachar Hills district, where violence perpetrated by the outlawed Black Widow or Jewel Gorlosa faction of the Dima Halam Daogah (DHD-J) has compelled the railways to suspend its operations on the Lumding-Silchar section since May 12.

The DHD(J) alone has been responsible for killing at least 50 persons in the North Cachar Hills district since January, which included several contract labourers engaged in the broad gauge conversion work of the railways and the East-West Corridor project of the National Highway Authority of India.

The report says while 17 security force personnel had lost their lives in Assam during 2004, the figure went up to 27 during 2007. The figure was even more — 32 — in 2006.

The situation, however, is worse in Manipur where 130 civilians were killed by various militant groups in 2007. The figure was 88 in 2004. The number of violent incidents in the state went up from 478 in 2004 to 584 in 2007.

Heading: IIM-C releases OBC offer letters - Indian Express
Content:
Here's good news for ex-servicemen. The corporate world has discovered in this community a great pool of human resource to recruit from. Disclosing this here on Friday, MM Pallam Raju, Union Minister of State for Defence said seeing the keen interest of the corporate world in recruiting more ex-servicemen, the defence ministry has directed the Directorate-General (resettlement) to not only coordinate with the corporate world but also prepare defence personnel for post-retirement employment.

"The corporate world has shown tremendous interest in recruiting more and more ex-servicemen. This is because they (the ex-servicemen) are disciplined, skilled, energetic and are very good organisers," the minister said.

He said the DG (Resettlement) was already working on creating a database of all ex-servicemen and then make it available for the private sector. "The DG (R) has also taken up schemes to impart special skills to the serving personnel nearing retirement," Raju said. He was here to inaugurate a pension adalat for ex-servicemen.

"Last year the DG (R) had set a target of getting re-employment for about 40,000 ex-servicemen. But at the end of the year we found that there was a direct demand for over 65,000 persons, who actually found jobs mostly in the private and corporate sector," the minister said.

Over 60,000 persons retire from the defence forces every year in the country. "Gone are the days when the ex-serviceman was only fit to be a security officer or a guard in different organisations. He is today the most sought-after person by every sector, be it the public sector or the private sector," Raju added.

He said the zilla sainik boards and state sainik boards have been directed to coordinate and work as partners in creating a nationwide network where ex-servicemen can not only solve their post-retirement grievances faster but also find employment through the new initiatives.

"This huge resource base must be used for the growth of the country. The hospitality sector and the service sector are already giving preference to the ex-serviceman over the ordinary job-seeker," he said.

Heading: Five wildlife sanctuaries to get tiger reserve status - Indian Express
Content:
After a series of hurdles, IIM-Calcutta finally released offer letters to OBC candidates on Friday. Although the Calcutta High Court had earlier stayed the admission of OBC students on May 14, the impasse was cleared by the Supreme Court after a few days allowing the institute to carry on with its admission process. IIM-C conducted the group discussion and personal interview on May 15 but was waiting for a go-ahead from the Ministry of Human Resources Development (MHRD) before releasing its final list.

"MHRD has enclosed a copy of the Supreme Court ruling with the official letter and asked the institute to go ahead with the admission process," said the chief administrative officer of IIM-Calcutta, Dinesh Varma. Since the academic session will start from June 23, it is high time the offer letters were sent to the students, an IIM-C official added.

However, since the instructions from the ministry are not very clear, the offer letters are provisional — the candidates in question were asked to sign a statement declaring that their admissions would be null and void in case of any legal complications.

This year, out of 318 students, nine students will be admitted under the OBC quota to IIM-C for the postgraduate diploma course in business management.

Heading: Arunachal may come under Unified Command - Indian Express
Content:
Five wildlife sanctuaries in the country will soon be getting tiger reserve status for better management of the conservation plans for the big cat in its core habitat.

The National Tiger Conservation Authority, in a meeting held recently, has given an "in-principle" approval to four new reserves, a senior official said on Friday. These are Sunabeda Tiger Reserve in Orissa, Shahyadri Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, Pilibhit Tiger Reserve in Uttar Pradesh and Ratapani Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh. All the four states had submitted proposals to the Union Environment Ministry seeking tiger reserve status for the wildlife sanctuaries and national parks.

The authority also accorded approval to a proposal from Karnataka to treat Nagarahole National Park, which was a part of Bandipur Tiger Reserve, as a separate reserve for the big cat, the official said. Getting tiger reserve status will help the parks secure more Central funds for protection of the endangered animal. The four new tiger reserves are in addition to the eight parks for which clearance was given in January.

Heading: Cong old guard seeks to build new bridges to Rahul - Indian Express
Content:
Arunachal Pradesh is likely to be placed under a Unified Command for better synergisation and coordination in the fight against terror.

A proposal for having a Unified Command comprising Army, the state police and all other security agencies on the lines of the ones in Jammu and Kashmir and neighbouring Assam was sent by the governor, general J J Singh (retd) , who has special power under Article 371-H, to the Cabinet for deliberation.

"The law and order situation in the state was by and large peaceful except in Tirap and Changlang districts adjacent to Nagaland but there was a danger of spilling over of the activities of the undergrounds elsewhere," the former Army chief said on Friday.

Tirap and Changlang have already been declared disturbed under the Armed Forces Special Power Act in view of activities of terrorists from neighbouring states who also use this as a corridor for transit to and from from their camps across the Myanmar border.

"If we allow them to continue their activities, we would have a situation which is certainly not good for our country," he said.

Heading: Rotate Scheduled Caste seats, says Delimitation Commission - Indian Express
Content:
It is not only HRD Minister Arjun Singh who keeps on trying to build on his loyalty quotient to make up for his controversial remarks about the decision-making process in the party, the Congress is witnessing a virtual scramble for the coveted loyalist tag.

The latest to join the "Hail Rahul" brigade are former Union Ministers Aslam Sher Khan and PK Thungan, former Uttar Pradesh Governor Romesh Bhandari, former Madhya Pradesh PCC chief Subhash Yadav, and ex-MPs Dilip Singh Bhuria and Pratap Bhanu Sharma. They were among the 180 senior Congress leaders who met at the Parliament annexe on Thursday to deliberate on how to "strengthen" the hands of AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi.

While many are quick to dismiss them as "spent force", a section in the party believes it was manifestation of growing unease among the party's old guards who find themselves sidelined as Rahul builds his own team in the party.

Since his appointment as AICC general secretary last September, Rahul has been trying to strengthen his hold on the organisation, increasingly taking part in decision-making processes like distribution of tickets in Assembly elections, making key organisational appointments and devising the party's electoral strategy.

Even though Rahul calls up AICC general secretaries to seek updates about the developments in their respective states of which they are in-charge, they remain virtually in the dark about his plans, say sources.

Although senior leaders like Motilal Vora, Janardan Dwivedi, Margaret Alva, Mohsina Kidwai and Mukul Wasnik continue to enjoy the confidence of Congress president Sonia Gandhi, they do not figure in Rahul's core team, say sources. Similarly, senior ministers like Pranab Mukherjee, AK Antony and Shivraj Patil continue to be part of the Congress president's core team, but do not figure in Rahul's team of advisors.

When an official press release announced the appointment of eight coordinators to work with AICC general secretaries and in-charges of states, the general secretaries concerned were caught unawares. Rahul had a big role in the appointment of coordinators, say sources.

The elevation of AICC secretary Rajiv Shukla, who was appointed coordinator to work with AICC general secretary BK Hari Prasad, is attributed to his growing proximity to the Amethi MP. Former Assam PCC chief Pawan Kumar Ghatowar, who was appointed coordinator to work with Ajay Makan, is perceived to be close to Salman Khursheed who is learnt to have made his way into Rahul's team recently, say sources.

Many senior leaders and ministers, who played a key role in the decision-making process earlier, feel sidelined because they are no more consulted. Arjun Singh is learnt to have been seeking an appointment with Rahul for several weeks but was disappointed, say sources. Talking to The Indian Express, Singh, however, denied he ever sought any appointment with the Amethi MP. While quitting the party, Akhilesh Das had complained that he had been seeking an appointment with Rahul for four months.

At Rahul's behest, a panel of senior Congress leaders has been interviewing Youth Congress leaders from every state; these candidates are then assigned different responsibilities in the respective state units. Such interviews have already been conducted in over half a dozen states, say sources.

When Rahul was to visit Karnataka as part of his "discover India" tour, even AICC general secretary in charge of the state Prithviraj Chavan remained clueless about his itinerary until about 24 hours before the Amethi MP landed there, say sources.

Only AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh, Rahul's personal assistant Kanishka Singh, Youth Congress president Ashok Tanwar and a few others close to Rahul were aware of his travel plans. Youth Congress candidates, selected by the above-mentioned panel, had been sent to the state in advance though.

As the writing on the wall is getting clear, many old warhorses have been anxiously watching the unfolding of new power dynamics in the party. But those left out in the old scheme of things see in it an opportunity. Incidentally, most in the second category come from Madhya Pradesh, which was evident from the list of leaders present in Thursday's meeting at the Parliament annexe.

Heading: In election year, Cong plans to rice to occasion with YSR idea - Indian Express
Content:
The Delimitation Commission has recommended for rotation of Scheduled Caste constituencies. "Some of the constituencies were reserved for several decades. This should not happen, there should be some methodology," Delimitation Commission chairman Justice Kuldip Singh said here on Friday.

"The Commission recommends that the Government consider incorporating suitable provisions in law to provide for rotation in the reservation of SC constituencies," he said, adding that it was up to the Government to decide on it.

Constituencies, Justice Singh said, should be "redrawn after every ten years". "The Commission is firmly of the view that delimitation should be carried out after every Census, so that readjustment of the constituencies, including changes and alterations, are not too extensive and the value of electoral vote remains more or less of equal weight," he said.

The Election Commission, meanwhile, said it was ready to hold the next Lok Sabha elections as per redrawn constituencies "any time after August 31". "Our electoral rolls, revised according to the newly delimited constituencies, will be ready by August 31," Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswamy told reporters on Friday.

Heading: Hugo Chavez seeks better ties with India - Indian Express
Content:
Concerned about the fallout of galloping inflation in an election year, the Congress is planning to replicate the Andhra Pradesh Government's Rs 2 per kg rice scheme in all states where the party is in power. The issue came up for discussion at a meeting of party general secretaries, including Rahul Gandhi, at the AICC headquarters here on Thursday.

In its manifesto for Karnataka Assembly election too, the Congress had announced 25 kg of rice at Rs 2 per kg to BPL cardholders, apart from other freebies.

It was, however, outdone by the BJP, which announced the same price for rice, but remained silent on its quantum while indicating that it could be more than that of the Congress.

Senior Congress leaders believed different political parties would try to outdo one another in offering freebies in the ensuing elections as well and, therefore, it wanted to take the lead by being the first to announce heavily subsidised foodgrains like rice or wheat in party-ruled states, according to sources.

As for the states where the Congress is not in power, the party is likely to announce the same in its manifesto. There would be further discussion on this issue at the next meeting of AICC general secretaries on Monday, said sources.

According to the deliberations at Thursday's meeting, respective state units of the Congress would be asked to identify issues that could be raised in the Opposition-ruled states. Suggestions would be invited from all state units as to how to go about publicising the achievements of the UPA Government.

Meanwhile, AICC spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi said on Friday that no timeline could be set for containing inflation as it was driven by global prices of oil and other commodities. This came in response to a question at a press briefing about Prime Minister Manmohan Singh changing the timeline for containing inflation.

Last month, the PM had told reporters at Rashtrapati Bhavan that the Government's measures to contain inflation would start showing results "in a couple of weeks".

Addressing a function to mark the completion of four years of the UPA Government on Thursday, the PM, however, changed the timeline to "8-10 weeks".

Heading: BJP demands apology from Home Minister - Indian Express
Content:
Venezuela President Hugo Chavez has conveyed his desire to strengthen and diversify bilateral relations with India, a Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson said on Friday.

This was conveyed in a meeting between Chavez and MoS for External Affairs Anand Sharma during the latter's three-day visit to Venezuela from May 18 to 20.

"The two nations discussed the exploration in Carbobo 1 and Junin Norte oilfields, which received a positive response. India has also invited Venezuela to invest in greenfield refinery projects in partnership with Oil PSUs in an integrated petrochemical complex. Chavez has confirmed his country's desire to develop a durable and multi-faceted partnership, especially in the fields of energy, science & technology, agriculture, and pharmaceuticals, including generics," an official statement said.

The next India-Venezuela Joint Commission meeting will be held in New Delhi later this year.

"A road map for enhancing strategic and enduring cooperation between both the countries in a various sectors, including agriculture, energy and renewable energy, infrastructure and transfer of technology was discussed during the meeting, attended by Venezuelan Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Energy and Petroleum, Light Industries and Commerce and Science & Technology," the Spokesperson said.

Chavez also expressed high regard for Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, President Pratibha Patil and Congress president Sonia Gandhi, the spokesperson said.

Sharma had detailed discussions with Foreign Minister Nicolas Maduro where they reviewed various regional and global issues of mutual concern like setting up of alternative financial and monetary architecture mechanism through institutions such as the Bank of South, regional development initiatives and other matters.

A gamut of bilateral relations was reviewed in a luncheon meeting where Venezuelan ministers of Culture, S&T, Education and Higher Education and vice-ministers of Light Industries and Commerce & Tourism also participated.

The Venezuelan side thanked India for its offer to set-up an IT Centre of Excellence in Venezuela.

Heading: Coast Guard thinks fishermen seeking better catch in Pak waters - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP has demanded an "unqualified apology" from Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil for equating Sarabjit Singh with Parliament attack convict Afzal Guru. The opposition party also expressed outrage about Patil "lying" about the issue of opening detention centres for illegal immigrants.

"Nobody in the country and outside raised any demand for clemency for Afzal on any ground. But the Home Minister wants to justify dillydallying on Afzal's execution by giving a completely absurd twist to the issue," stated party spokesperson Prakash Javadekar. He added that if Patil did not apologise, the PM should direct him to do so: "If the Home Minister fails to comply, then sack him."

The BJP spokesperson also contested Patil's claim that the Centre had not issued any direction to Rajasthan regarding the opening of detention centres for illegal Bangladeshi immigrants, saying that he had "documentary evidence to prove the Home Ministry's role."

Heading: Heavy security in place for Amarnath Yatra - Indian Express
Content:
The absence of hi-tech navigation aids was for long thought to be the main cause for scores of Gujarat fishermen straying into Pakistani waters and often getting arrested. But, with the problem showing no signs of abating despite many boats acquiring global positioning systems (GPS), the Coast Guard believes many fishermen are deliberately entering Pakistani waters as the catch is better there. The Coast Guard, therefore, has written to the Gujarat Government to help fight the problem, and has also taken it up with the Union Home Ministry to tackle what has been a niggling problem in the India-Pakistan relationship.

"We have taken up this case with the Gujarat Government so that such cases can be curbed," Coast Guard Inspector-General (Western region) Rajendra Singh told The Indian Express. "We even have boats patrolling the maritime border round-the-clock to keep a tab on boats straying into Pakistani waters," he added. Coast Guard sources said until April this year, the force had brought back about 350 Indian boats that had strayed into Pakistani waters compared to 850 all of last year. "These boats stray as deep as 50 km inside Pakistani waters," a senior Coast Guard official. "But it's not as if the fishermen don't know that they have strayed into Pakistani waters.," he said.

Fishing industry officials in Gujarat, which has 30,000 registered mechanised boats and a coastline of 1,600 km, confirmed the Coast Guard's suspicions. "Fish along the Gujarat coast have become less compared to the Pakistani coast where water is less polluted and has better quality tiger prawns and other varieties of fishes. Also, fishermen have to recover costs. One deep sea trip costs around Rs 90,000, so fishermen take the risk of straying into Pakistani waters," said Manishbhai Lodhari, Gujarat secretary of the National Fish Workers Forum.

Saying that they were yet to receive the Coast Guard letter, Gujarat Fisheries department secretary Anil Sutaria said they were already working on the issue. "To avert this problem (of straying), the state Government is taking up a Rs 150-crore project wherein GPS systems will be installed on all 30,000 small and big registered boats," Sutaria said. "Through this, the fishermen can be tracked centrally and warned. They too can contact us in case of emergency," he said.

In the net

Indian boats brought back from Pakistan waters

• In 2004 200

• In 2005 503

• In 2006 540

Fishermen languishing in jails

• Pakistan 400 Indians

• India 100 Pakistanis

Heading: Pak frees 99 Indian prisoners - Indian Express
Content:
Around 10,000 securitymen drawn from various agencies will be deployed to ensure the safety of pilgrims during this year's Amarnath Yatra, which officially starts on June 18. Around five lakh pilgrims are expected to take part in the two-month yatra.

A recent meeting of police and security officers, chaired by Jammu and Kashmir DGP Kuldeep Khuda, reviewed the security arrangements in detail. Sources said around 50 battalions of police and paramilitary men would be deployed in the Valley during the yatra.

While the state police and CRPF would guard various pilgrim camps at Pahalgam and Baltal, the BSF would keep vigil along various routes leading to the base camps.

Besides, three battalions of the Army would keep a vigil on the upper reaches of the route. "We will keep a proactive approach to ensure that the yatra passes off peacefully," said Prabakar Tripathi, the CRPF spokesman, in Srinagar.

On Thursday, DIG South Kashmir Muneer Khan said the authorities had taken strict measures to ensure that no one entered the cave before official commencement of the yatra.

The Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB) has also asked pilgrims not to move towards the cave before the yatra begins.

"Police teams have been deployed at various points... even personnel deployed for yatra duty would not be allowed to have darshan before the scheduled date," Khan said.

Meanwhile, environmentalists and the state Pollution Control Board have expressed fear that the huge inflow of yatris will harm the ecology of the area.

They have also highlighted the fact that there is still no wastage disposal system along the yatra route. But Governor Lt Gen S K Sinha (retd), who also heads the SASB, said all necessary precautions were being taken to preserve the fragile ecology of the area.

Heading: MiG-21 crashes due to technical snag; pilot escapes - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan on Friday freed 96 Indian fishermen and three other prisoners from a jail here as a goodwill gesture close on the heels of External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's visit to this country. The three prisoners had been held in Pakistan for at least 20 years, past their terms.

The move came two days after India and Pakistan signed an agreement on granting consular access to each other's citizens held in jails of the two countries. The Indian fishermen and other prisoners will be taken from Karachi to Lahore before being handed over to Indian authorities at the Wagah border on Saturday, officials said.

Indian authorities had earlier confirmed the nationality of the fishermen and other prisoners.

Shortly after Mukherjee arrived in Pakistan on May 20 for a meeting with his counterpart Shah Mehmood Qureshi to review the composite dialogue process, Pakistan's Interior Ministry had announced that the 96 Indian fishermen and three other prisoners would be released as a goodwill gesture.

The fishermen were arrested after they strayed into Pakistan's territorial waters. Hundreds of fishermen from both countries are arrested every year by India's Coast Guard and Pakistan's Maritime Security Agency for accidentally drifting into each other's territorial waters.

India and Pakistan have initiated steps for the speedy release of fishermen as part of confidence-building measures between the two sides.

Heading: Gurjjar stir turns violent, 6 dead - Indian Express
Content:
A MiG-21 fighter aircraft made an emergency landing at the Indian Air Force's Bagdogra airbase in the early hours on Friday and within minutes, burst into flames.

The pilot, Squadron Leader Falguni Roy, had ejected safely after detecting a fault in the undercarriage, which prompted her to go for the belly landing.

The aircraft had taken off at 10 am from the Bagdogra airbase on a routine sortie. But it was back within half-an-hour.

The fire-fighters of the Indian Air Force doused the flames within 15 minutes and the runway was cleared for resumption of civilian flights. An inquiry had been ordered into the accident.

The MiG-21 has a history of crashes, due to which it has acquired the sobriquet "flying coffins".

Earlier this year, a MiG-27 crashed near the Air Force station at Hashimara in West Bengal's Jalpaiguri district.

Heading: Advani calls Sharad, Nitish for talks to sort out BJP-JD(U) ties - Indian Express
Content:
Once again a Gurjjar protest turned horribly violent in Rajasthan leaving at least six persons dead. While authorities claim six persons including a police constable died along the railway track at Bayana in Bharatpur, where the Gurjjars had gathered to protest on Friday morning, sources said the toll could be higher.

Friday's trouble comes a week ahead of the first anniversary of the police firing on Gurjjar agitators in the state and subsequent violence that claimed 26 lives and sparked off tension between the Meenas and the Gurjjars. The Gurjjars are demanding Scheduled Caste status.

The trouble started around 1 pm on Friday when hundreds of Gurjjars gathered near the Dungaria railway station in support of a 'rail roko' call given by Rajasthan Gurjar Arakashan Sangarsh Samiti leader Kirori Singh Bainsla. The police tried to use teargas to disperse the crowds, followed by a couple of rounds fired in the air. When the crowd refused to budge, they fired at the protesters killing five of them — some sources put the toll at seven.

Soon, the protesters caught hold of police constable Bhola Ram and bludgeoned him to death. Those injured in the melee have been referred to hospitals in Hindon. Reports said Col Baisala had gone on a "maun vrat" following the firing.

"The mob threw stones and did not disperse even after police lobbed teargas shells," Principal Home Secretary V S Singh said in Jaipur. Later, at an emergency Cabinet meeting state Home Minister Gulab Chand Kataria condemned the timing of the protests, coming hardly a week after the blasts in the state capital. Kataria said the protesters violated Section 144 of the CrPC which had been imposed in the area two days back.

The area has been cordoned off, with RAF and police personnel stepping back from the area. But the protestors are not allowing anyone, including the police, near the track now. Trains on the Delhi-Mumbai route had been diverted in the afternoon itself avoiding possible delays.

Meanwhile, the Centre on Friday rushed paramilitary forces to the state. Six companies of Rapid Action Force (RAF) and three companies of Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) have been sent to the state and stationed around the trouble-affected region of Bharatpur. The RAF units have been moved from Aligarh while CRPF reinforcements would come from Delhi, sources said. Two Mi-17 helicopters of the Indian Air Force (IAF) have been put on standby.

A Home Ministry statement said the Centre was in regular touch with the state Government and was keeping a close watch on the events.

With PTI

Heading: UP chief secretary out, replaced by Atul Gupta - Indian Express
Content:
Taking the initiative to put the BJP ties with JD(U) back on the rails, NDA prime ministerial candidate L K Advani has invited party allies Sharad Yadav and Nitish Kumar for talks on May 25. BJP president Rajnath Singh has also been invited. The talks, according to highly-placed sources, would be held at Advani's Prithviraj Road residence.

The relations between the two NDA partners have been of late passing through a rough patch. To start with, it was the poaching of JD(U) leaders by the BJP in Karnataka, particularly of S R Bommai's son Basvaraj Bommai, which triggered a boycott of floor co-ordination meetings by the JD(U) held during the Budget session of Parliament. The JD(U) grouse was that the BJP was out to finish it in various states by engineering defections from its ranks.

Though Advani tried to undo the damage by undertaking to prevent any poaching in future, the BJP refusal to accommodate JD(U) seat claims for a tie-up during Karnataka Assembly polls only made the things worse.

"The BJP has torn alliance norms to shreds," JD(U) president Sharad Yadav exclaimed in frustration and retaliated by fielding over 70 candidates for the 224-member Assembly.

In the midst of this has developed the Bihar crisis, which, if unresolved, has the potential to redefine political alignments in the state. At one level, both JD(U) and BJP are facing internal convulsions following a reshuffle of the council of ministers by Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar last month.

A revolt is simmering within the JD(U) with 22 of its 88 MLAs involved in dissidence. The problem in the BJP is far more serious with some three dozen of the 55 MLAs seeking removal of Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Kumar Modi as leader of the party's legislature group and refusing to settle down for anything short of this.

Their charge: he is a puppet in Nitish's hands. Therefore, he is being dubbed unfit to effectively protect the BJP interests in the Government.

Taking up cudgels on behalf of the anti-Modi elements, veteran party leader Kailashpati Mishra has submitted a proposal to the party high command to pull out of the Bihar Government and lend outside support to Nitish. This, according to him, is the best way to save the party. Nitish is said to be having a grand ambition to dispense with the BJP in future and be on his own through a different social alliance by taking the 18 per cent Muslims to his party fold. His designs are evident from the fact that he has maintained a safe distance from the BJP, staying away from Advani's book launch function as well as NDA chief ministers' conclave. Alongside, he has pushed a 10 per cent programme targeting Muslims and wooed non-Yadav OBCs through a variety of measures, including reservations in panchayat bodies.

There are also reports of an attempt to break the RJD by working on Rajya Sabha member Subhash Yadav, brother-in-law of Railways Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, amidst attempts to woo Lok Janshakti Party president Ram Vilas Paswan.

While Nitish works on his grand design, a sudden pull-out by the BJP implies an unforeseen turn in the plot. Once the saffron party decides to sit outside, it would practically claim the space of the Opposition, save its upper-caste base and attract disgruntled elements from all parties, including JD(U). Nitish has to prevent this and ensure a continuation of Modi in his post.

However, Advani has to keep the NDA afloat to match the UPA in the next Lok Sabha polls. There being a mutual need on either side, the meeting is expected to yield fruitful results for both.

Heading: 40 pc of cultivable area in Bundelkhand not sown: report - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Prashant Kumar Mishra sought voluntary retirement on Thursday evening and was promptly replaced with Industrial Development Commissioner Atul Gupta, a 1974 batch IAS officer. Government sources said Mishra, who was due to retire in August, was asked to seek voluntary retirement.

"I have three more months to go, but I have taken this decision for personal reasons," Mishra said. "What I have done is to protect the dignity of the institution and the service and I have no regrets," he hastened to add. In a letter to IAS officers, he said: "What is more important is not how long you stayed on the crease of life but how fast you scored. Always keep up the principles of life which are more important than the mundane pecuniary material benefits of the service."

Officially, there was no word from the Government on Mishra's unceremonious exit. "What triggered this is not clear, but it was on the cards," an official said.

The corridors of the secretariat in Lucknow had been rife for sometime with speculation about the possible fallout of the tension between the Chief Secretary and Cabinet Secretary Sashank Shekhar Singh.

A senior official said: "Though the Chief Secretary was officially designated as the head of the state administration by the state Government last February, there was no change in the de facto power structure in the bureaucracy. The Cabinet Secretary remained the real boss".

Another officer said Mishra was "not playing his role at the Cabinet meetings as desired by the chief minister". In the last meeting, out of 20 items, he came up with a different view on most. "In today's cabinet note too, he disagreed with the government view on about 15 items". This irked the CM, he added. Sources in the Government said Mishra was being considered for appointment to one of the many Government set-ups.

Mishra's last bow

Before demitting office, Mishra wrote a letter to all Principal Secretaries to UP government today saying: "He who would accomplish little must sacrifice little... he who would achieve much must sacrifice much and he who would attain highly must sacrifice highly." The missive goes on to thank all officers who stood by him and "extended all cooperation in discharge of affairs of state". Profusely quoting Shakespeare, Mishra says: "Life is never a straight line... not a bed of roses nor is it Midsummer Night's Dream. At times it becomes a Tempest or a Winter's Tale or you can take it As You Like It... what is more important in life is not how long you have stayed in the crease but how fast you have scored in life... always keep up the principles of life which are more important that the sundry pecuniary benefits of service."

Heading: Prime Minister’s childhood friend from Pakistan arrives with memories, gifts - Indian Express
Content:
Even as UP Chief Minister Mayawati and Congress MPs continue to trade charges on the issue of development, the drought in the Bundelkhand region comprising 13 districts from UP and MP has meant that an average of about 40 per cent of the cultivable area was not sown during 2007-08.

As a result, according to a report prepared by a high-level inter-ministerial Central team which visited these districts during December 2007 and April 2008, there was doubling of distress migration in the last year with people demanding increase in the employment days under the UPA Government's flagship NREG.

The report prepared under the chairmanship of Dr JS Samra, the CEO of National Rainfed Area Authority, has recommended a package of over Rs 8,000 crore on "definite basis" to tackle the worsening situation. The report recommends a little under Rs 4,000 crore for UP region and little over Rs 4,000 crore for MP region of Bundelkhand.

"Out of four years, moderate to severe agricultural drought occurred for two-four years in the 13 districts of Bundelkhand. Net sown area in 2007-08 ranged from 15 to 80 per cent of normal — with an average of 60 per cent — and 22 per cent decline in grain production was observed," says the report.

In fact, the report points out that 75 per cent of Mahoba district (UP) and 78 per cent of Tikamgrah district (MP) of the region could not be sown in 2007-08 due to severe drought conditions. No wonder, the migration has particularly shot up last year, notes the report.

"Normally, 15-20 per cent of the labour out migrate from Bundelkhand after wheat sowing, and this figure was reported to be 40 per cent during the drought of 2007-08," records the report pointing to the widespread demand for increasing the employment days under NREG.

"Hydrological drought was evident from 15 to 47 per cent decline in the filling of reservoirs in Madhya Pradesh, 28 to 64 per cent in UP over three years, 70 per cent dried up tanks, ponds and steep fall in ground watertable," says the report submitted to the Centre on April 15, 2008. The situation is so bad that the depletion of groundwater and loss in the fertility of livestock, which happens to be a substantial source of livelihood in the region, due to unavailability of fodder that it "may recover in four-five years" only presuming normal rainfall, says the report.

Even as the Central Government sits on this report, Bundelkhand politics is going to take centre stage with Madhya Pradesh heading for Assembly elections later this year. The MP Chief Minister is already crying foul against the lack of enough Central support. Similarly, UP CM Mayawati is also likely to train her guns on the Centre for its apathy.

Heading: CPM meet to analyse Bengal poll debacle - Indian Express
Content:
If all goes well, "Mohna te Ali di jodi" will be back again, as Raja Mohammed Ali from Pakistan arrived here on Friday to meet his friend, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

Carrying childhood memories in his heart and a fistful of earth from his village, Ali, 70, says he feels as energised and young at the thought of meeting his friend as he did when he and Singh — "Mohna" to him — played marbles together. People of Gah village in Asli Chakwal often referred to them as "Mohna te Ali di jodi".

While there are loads of gifts for the PM — a "Chakwali jutti", pictures of his native place, Katasraj temples and Singh's marksheets from Class I to IV, and water from "our primary school" — he has also brought old pranks to share with his buddy. "Our teacher often beat me up for stealing dry fruits from Mohna's pockets in class," he says.

Ali has not sought any appointment from the PM, but is confident that his friend would find time to meet him. "I will meet bhabhiji and their children, if 'Mohna' is busy." He says the entire village in Pakistan wants Singh to visit his native place. "There was jubilation when 'Mohna' became the PM. The whole village is eager to see him at least once," he says, adding two schools and two dispensaries in the village have been named after Singh.

Ali had applied for a visa several times, but got lucky only now. He plans to be in India till July 15 and wants to meet his other friends in Punjab as well.

While he and his nephew Haji Ahmed were received by the staff and students of DAV Public School at Attari Border on Friday, he is looking forward to the kind of reception he will get at the PM's house.
